utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone, I say especially today to the technicians. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I spoke a special welcome to the technicians because of their efforts to restore LiveNote, and it's working well for everyone, apart from the Bench, who has no LiveNote at the moment. So if we would need to scroll back, we have to seek the assistance of the registrar and/or the legal officer. Mr. Tieger, are you ready to continue the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, as I said before, it looks already like a routine when I remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony, but I immediately add that this is, of course, not a routine matter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, the Court has set aside additional time today in an effort to maximise the possibility of completing your examination-in-chief. Toward that end, I will not be directing your attention to all the documents that you have selected, nor necessarily all of the highlights within those documents. And in addition, I hope we can move as quickly as possible through such documents as government sessions. And finally, I would ask, as I did yesterday, and as you did yesterday, to try to keep your answers as concise as possible. If we could turn first, then, to tab 136, the minutes of a meeting of 15 May 1992 of the National Security Council and the government -- well, it says: "And the Serbian Republic of BH." That document is on screen. Mr. Treanor, you've highlighted two sentences that appear in the lower half of the first page: "It was agreed to maintain and establish the positions in Sarajevo, and to defend the occupied territory, which is a priority task. It has been agreed to provide a war report on a daily basis."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I think that's fairly self-explanatory. I'd just like to point out, however, that I believe this is the last record we have of a session of the National Security Council --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, to interrupt, but there appears to be a problem. Mr. Krajisnik is not getting the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's see whether Mr. Krajisnik is on the right channel. Mr. Krajisnik, did you miss everything that was said until now, or did you by mistake change channels?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I didn't understand anything you were saying, but I have channel 6 here, in which I'm receiving Serbian interpretation. However, I'm not getting any interpretation. All right. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krajisnik, since you missed not many words, but at least some words, I think we just started with the examination, at least the substance of the examination. All the rest that was spoken this morning was about practical matters. But, Ms. Loukas, I take it that there's no need to consult with your client? He missed --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: No, there isn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He missed five minutes. Okay. Then we proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, you were just explaining that you believe this was the last record of the -- that you have of the session of the National Security Council.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is the last record that we have of a session of the National Security Council. After this date, we have independent minutes of meetings of the government, and we have no more record of any sessions of the National Security Council. It would therefore appear that after this date, the National Security Council lapsed. I would remind the Court that the expanded Presidency of three members was formed three days before. We didn't see the minutes of the first session of that body, but at that body were present not only the three members of the Presidency, that is, Dr. Karadzic and Dr. Koljevic and Plavsic, but also Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. Djeric. Those five individuals formed the core, as it were, of the National Security Council. So they seemed to be meeting independently under a different title. I would also point out that there's a handwritten notation indicating that these are the minutes of the 10th Session, presumably 10th Joint Session of the National Security Council and the government. This is in fact a record of the 12th meeting that we know of, indicating that the -- there's some confusion in the enumeration and that the total number of sessions that were held of this body is not precisely known to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn next to tab 137, the minutes of a meeting of the --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we do that -- oh, okay. I think Mr. Krajisnik has having some difficulty finding that particular document that we were just dealing with. But he's okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You by now have found the relevant document, Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the beginning, I didn't know exactly which binder the document was in, and that's why I couldn't find the document. My apologies to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On screen now are the minutes of a meeting of the government of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, held on 18 May 1992. Turn to page 2 of that document. You've highlighted two portions, the first a sentence which is enumerated number 4: "Proposing solutions for giving aid, i.e., 30 temporary loans to Crisis Staff." And the second at the bottom under AD-2: "It was concluded that aid be given to the Novo Sarajevo and Hadzici Crisis Staffs and that the amount of aid be determined according to the situation in these municipalities."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that's self-explanatory and I'd just like to point out that this is the -- a session only of the government. From this point on we see the government meeting separately, no longer with the National Security Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, turning to tab 138. That contains a meeting of May 21st, 1992. It's the minutes of a meeting of the government of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Turning to page 2, Mr. Treanor, you've highlighted two sentences in the middle of the page. I'm sorry. That would be page 3, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The first reads: "It is agreed that a committee for placing the refugees into other areas should be formed." The second: "With regards to this, it was emphasised that in dialogue with Serbia, it should be insisted that the Serb refugees from Serbia returned and settled in republics the Muslims had left from."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. The wording is a bit peculiar. However, it does reflect the language used in the original. I can only point out that there is a white space in the original between the words "in" and "republics." It's possible that the word "portions" or "parts," something like that, was supposed to be in there. But in any case, the reference seems to be to Serbs who had left BH to go to Serbia, and the idea being to return them to the Bosnian Serb Republic, to live in areas that had been abandoned by Muslims. Let me put it another way: In which Muslims were no longer living.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we turn next to tab 142, the minutes of a meeting of the Presidency on 31 May 1992. And this document, Mr. Treanor, you've highlighted the first paragraph, which states that: "On 31 May 1992, the 2nd Session of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina was held." And then indicates the attendance by members of the Presidency, Dr. Karadzic, Dr. Plavsic, and Dr. Koljevic, and the president of the Assembly of Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Momcilo Krajisnik." And you've highlighted the last sentence of the minutes, and I should indicate for the record the minutes only contain four short paragraphs. This is the fourth: "After the discussion, the Presidency adopted the decision on the establishment of war presidencies in municipalities during war or an imminent threat of war."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document is notable for several reasons. First of all, I would point out that the indication that this is the 2nd Session of the Presidency is inserted by hand. It is indeed the record -- it is indeed the second session for which we have a record. The first session took place on the 12th of May. We did not see that, but again, Mr. Krajisnik was there, and at that session, the main item of business was to elect Dr. Karadzic the president of the Presidency, being elected to that position by his two colleagues on the Presidency. So whether, in fact, there was no intervening session between the 12th and the 31st, I can't say definitely. As we saw, there was a meeting of the National Security Council on the 15th. The enumeration of those present is a little confusing. It refers to members of the Presidency. In the original, Dr. Radovan Karadzic, Dr. Biljana Plavsic, Dr. Nikola Koljevic, and presidents of the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Mr. Momcilo Krajisnik. That could lead one to believe that Mr. Krajisnik was being included among the members. This is important in connection with the decision which is recorded in the last paragraph of this document, namely, the decision on the establishment of war presidencies in municipalities during war or in imminent threat of war. I think we're about to see that document. I will continue my discussion in connection with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the document to which Mr. Treanor refers is contained behind tab 143 entitled, "Decision on the formation of war presidencies in municipalities in times of war or the immediate threat of war." Highlighted on the first page of that document is Article 4, which indicates that: "The Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina shall appoint the Republic's representative who shall give professional and other assistance to war presidencies."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd also call attention to Article 5 as a substantive matter here, which provides that the war presidencies, when they're established, will in effect replace the Crisis Staffs, which had been operating. So much for the substantive nature of this document. If we could go back to the very beginning of the document and magnify the first paragraph right under 168. As the Court can see, this decision was adopted by the Presidency on the basis of Article 5, paragraph 6 and 7 of the Constitutional Law on the implementation of the constitution. This decision, in fact, bears the date of the 31st of May, and we have seen in the minutes of the Presidency session of that day a reflection of the fact that the Presidency did in fact adopt this decision on that day. However, the provisions under which it has been adopted -- let me rephrase that. The enactment of the provisions under which this decision has been adopted, that is, Article 5, paragraph 6 and 7, have not yet appeared in the official record. I think we're about to see that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That would be tab 144, Your Honour. The document on screen at the moment is the Law on amending the constitutional law for implementing the constitution of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Article 1 is highlighted.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would draw attention, first of all, to the very first paragraph, or the top of the document, even above that, the date, as we can see, the date of the gazette in which this decision was published is the 1st of June. The previous decision, by the way, was published in the gazette on the 8th of June, so it's a different edition of the gazette and a prior edition of the gazette. Now if we could go to the very bottom of the document. Could we have the next page? Yes. We can see the date here of this decision as the 2nd of June, which is obviously one day later than the date of publication, as stated in the gazette. Now if we can return to the body of the document, Article 1. We can see in the second part of that article, where it says: "After paragraph 5, new paragraphs 6 and 7 are added." These are new paragraphs to Article 5 of the constitutional law. And this is the provision which gives the Presidency the authority during a state of war to establish war presidencies in the municipalities, and these are the provisions on the basis of which the decision of the 31st of May was made, and made on the 31st of May. To remind the Court, the title of that document referred to the establishment of war presidencies in municipalities during an imminent threat of war or a state of war. It would appear from the fact that the decision on this matter was in fact adopted on the 31st of May, that the Presidency considered that the conditions set by this amendment were in fact present and they therefore adopted the decision, which would seem to leave open the possibility that there was an error in the drafting here and that it should read: During an imminent threat of war or a state of war, the Presidency may decide ... I would also point out that the number of this document, which is given at the bottom of the document, just above the date, is 03-509/92, whereas the number of the decision on the establishment of the war presidencies is 0 -- 03-512. It would appear that this amendment to the constitutional law was adopted prior to the decision on the establishment of war presidencies, which I think would be logical, since it forms the basis for that decision. However, as the Court can see, there's confusion in the dating and perhaps in the wording. The only other thing I can add at this point in relation to that issue is that we do have an original typed and signed copy of this law, a law which, by the way, was adopted by the Presidency itself, and that copy contains the same features that we've Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. mentioned here. That is, it has the same wording and it indeed does bear the date of the 2nd of June and is signed by Dr. Karadzic. Now I would draw the Court's attention to the first part of Article 1, which states that: "During a state of war, the Presidency is expanded with the following members: The president of the National Assembly and the prime minister of the government." Now, as we have seen, on the 31st of May, when the decision on the war presidencies was adopted, Mr. Krajisnik was in fact present and could be understood, from a reading of that document, to be included among the members of the Presidency. On that day, as I say, the Presidency, on the 31st of May, obviously considered that the condition for adopting the decision on war presidencies was present, which could lead one to conclude that they also considered that the condition necessary for the expansion of the Presidency to five members from three was also present, and that therefore, as of the 31st of May, Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. Djeric are also members of the Presidency. This five-member Presidency would, as I indicated earlier, contain the core members of the old National Security Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And do some of the subsequent documents, meetings of the Presidency, contain explicit references to Mr. Krajisnik as a member of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We will be seeing further documents which indicate precisely that. I would also draw the Court's attention to Appendix 19 in our report, which lists all the sessions of the Presidency of which we are aware, and indicating which members were present from that tabulation, it is apparent that Mr. Krajisnik attended every session of the Presidency for the rest of the year that we have a record of. It's on page 175 of the report. No, it's not. That's the National Security Council. It's on page 186 of the report, Appendix 25. From that tabulation, it's clear that Mr. Krajisnik was the only member of the Presidency that attended every session, of which we are aware, and in fact on at least one occasion, he chaired a session, in the absence of Dr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I disrupted our chronology slightly. I'd like to return to the 27th of May, 1992, and tab 32 of the intercept binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just in relation to this, that last question, and I just want to put a marker here. I think it's inappropriate for Mr. Tieger to be asking leading questions in such a contentious area, and I'd be objecting to any further leading in this area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that the presence of Mr. Krajisnik during meetings? Is that -- because the question was: "Do some of the subsequent documents, meetings of the Presidency, contain explicit reference to Mr. Krajisnik as a member --"

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: "As a member of the Presidency," that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the presence of Mr. Krajisnik during the meetings of the Presidency also a contentious issue?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: No. The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just his quality as a member of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Quite, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's clear, I take it, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Precisely, Your Honour. First of all, I don't consider that a leading question. It can be answered yes or no. And second, it was only a reference to the -- whether or not the particular document contained language to that effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, the document speaks about -- and the answer of the witness was about attendance, whether Mr. Krajisnik was present. I do understand that it's not his presence during meetings, but whether he formally was a member of the Presidency. I do understand that that's a contentious issue. So if that comes up again, I would say then would you please ask the witness in a non-leading way in that specific respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I will certainly follow the Court's guidance on that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Tab 32 of the intercept binder is next as I indicated. I momentarily overlooked that. That is a conversation between Mr. Krajisnik and General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But before doing so, may I just ask one question to you, Ms. Loukas, in order to know for sure what the position of the Defence is. Under tab 144, we see a text which is a law on amending constitutional law for implementing the constitution of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. In Article 1, it says: "During a state of war, the Presidency is expanded with the following members." Is it that -- is the contentious issue that there was a state of war, or is the contentious issue that this article would for other reasons not apply? I'm just trying to find out what the position of the Defence is. Was there no state of war or just this article for other reasons does not apply? What's your position in this respect?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Oh, sorry. In fact, Your Honour, it's a number of bases, and including this question of a state of war. But of course, at this stage, I would not be wanting to enumerate all of the bases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do we find them in the pre-trial brief or -- I mean, if -- would you ask questions to the witness in cross-examination or not? Because otherwise, it becomes a bit of a trial by surprise that --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Oh, indeed, Your Honour. I mean, the whole point, of course, is not trial by ambush by the Prosecution or anybody, but all I am saying is of course there will be questions directed to these issues, clearly, during cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I take it that under Rule 90(H), the position of the Defence will then be clear, because you have to put to the witness --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Oh, indeed, Your Honour. Of course, that refers, of course, to Your Honour's referring to the inclusion within the Rules of Brown and Dunne [phoen] and the putting of the case and those aspects. There's no question, of course, Your Honour, that those matters will be put.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we might need some patience until early April, but that's clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we can now play the intercept, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here we see Mr. Krajisnik dealing directly with General Mladic on certain issues, in particular, coordinating with the Ministry of Internal Affairs on behalf of General Mladic. The references to Tolimir and Manojlo are to two of the high-ranking officers on General Mladic's staff. There's a reference to Momo at a couple of points. It's possible that that could be a reference to Mr. Mandic, who we've met before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn to tab 145, and then subsequently, tab 146, the Defence Act, and then subsequently, the Law on the Army. If we could just quickly look at those. Tab 146, the Defence Act, on page 2. I'm sorry. That's a misleading reference, Your Honours, I apologise. Tab 145 is the Defence Act. At page 2 you highlighted Article 7, specifically, numbers 2, 3, and 6 of Article 7, which begins: "As part of organising preparations for defence, the president of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina shall..." And 2, 3, and 4 indicate: "Proclaim a state of emergency, imminent threat of war and war, order general and partial mobilisation." 3 is: "Command and control of the army both in peacetime and war." 6 is: "Define the basis for the organisation and size of the police force, issue orders for the deployment of the police in time of war," and it continues to the end of that number 6.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are provisions in this new law which was adopted by the Presidency on the 1st of June and published in the gazette on that same day. Emphasising here are provisions of that law that relate to the powers of the president of the republic. The Court will notice the reference to proclaiming a state of emergency, imminent threat of war, and war. The previous enactments, including the constitution and other legislation, had not specified who would perform this function. That could be because at the time the original documents were adopted on the 28th of February, it was foreseen that the republic would be part of the federal Yugoslav state, whose central federal organs would have the responsibility of making such declarations. As we did see, however, on the 15th of April, the acting presidents at the proposal of the National Security Council did in fact declare an imminent threat of war in the Bosnian Serb Republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The law on the army is contained and behind tab 146. And on page 24 of that document.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This law is adopted by the Presidency on the same day and contains a large number of provisions relating to the authority of the president in various military matters, including command and control and discipline.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And for the record, you've highlighted Article 173, Article 174, and at the bottom of the page, 175 continuing on to the next page, the first three paragraphs of the next page.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn next to tab 147, the minutes from the government meeting of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina held on June 1 1992. You have highlighted on the first page item number 1: "The government president has informed government members about the talks that took place at the joint meeting of Serbian Republic of BiH Presidency, Serbian Republic of BiH National Assembly chairman, Serbian Republic government president and Serbian Republic of BiH army Main Staff commander."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Moving on to tab 150. Your Honour, tab 150 contains the minutes from a government session held on 5 June 1992. And if we turn to page 2. Mr. Treanor, you've highlighted item number 1: "The government president has informed the government about the current issues of security situation in the republic. The information is based on the daily reports from the Ministry of the Interior."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. This excerpt and the one from the previous meeting that we saw would indicate, among other things, that the president of the government was, at the very least, privy to information that was coming into the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn next to tab 154, the meeting -- the minutes of a session of the government held on 9 June 1992. And if we could turn to page 2 of that document. Mr. Treanor, you've highlighted the second and third paragraphs of that page, the first of which begins: "The government has concluded that treatment and exchange of prisoners is a responsible and complex issue," and concludes: "Those instructions --" well, to clarify that, it goes on to talk about the preparation of instructions by the -- by certain organs, which would incorporate both domestic and international rules, and concludes: "Those instructions would be translated into English and sent to appropriate international bodies and especially to International Red Cross." And you've highlighted the paragraph thereafter, which reads: "Passing of these instructions and our commitment to legality and humanity by our republic should be used in anti-propaganda and propaganda activities in Yugoslavia and abroad."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is one of many references which occur in the government sessions to the issue of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn next to tab 155, which is headed, "Minutes of the 4th expanded meeting of the War Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina of 9 June 1992." And in that document, Mr. Treanor, you've highlighted the first three paragraphs, and then items 3, 4, 7, and 11 of the conclusions following a detailed discussion.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I would call the Court's attention to the fact that in this document, as in one of the previous documents we've seen, the number 4 for the enumeration of the session has been inserted by hand. And I would also call the Court's attention to the reference to the expanded meeting of the War Presidency of the Serbian Republic and to the list of attendees.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Paragraph 1, for the record, you've highlighted, is that list of attendees. Paragraph 2 indicates that General Mladic briefed the Presidency in detail about the overall situation in the Serbian army, and he figures on the quantities of weapons, ammunition, spare parts, reserves of oil and oil products, food and other resources. And paragraph 3 indicates that General Gvero reported on the situation in the area of the Banja Luka Corps.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was a meeting that was dominated by military affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And for the record, the enumerated conclusions that you highlighted are number 3, that the heavy artillery fire in the town be halted. Number 4, that a strong unit from Krajina be transferred to assist in fighting around Sarajevo. Number 7, that talks be arranged between the SBH delegation and the Presidency and the General Staff of the Socialist Republic of Yugoslavia, and number 11, instruct members of the Serbian army to abide by Geneva Conventions in their treatment of prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn to tab 156. Tab 156 contains the minutes --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Tab 156 contains the minutes of a government meeting of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina held on 10 June 1992. On page 2, Mr. Treanor, you've highlighted the first full paragraph. Sorry, page 3, which indicates that: "The Ministry of Justice should make a report about prisoners. This report should pay attention on treatment of civilian Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. population, prisoners of war, accommodation, food, et cetera. The report would be considered by the government, after which it would be submitted to the Presidency of the republic."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here again we see reference to discussion of the issue of prisoners. And the minister of justice, to remind the Court at this point, is Momcilo Mandic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, turning next to tab 157.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Tab 157 contains the minutes of the 5th Session of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of BH held during an imminent threat of war on 10 June 1992. That is the heading. And Mr. Treanor, on this first page, you've highlighted the first and second paragraphs. The first conclusion adopted is the -- and the eighth conclusion.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we see a variety of decisions adopted at the meeting. The decision referred to in point 8 is a decision which, in effect, replaces the previous decision that we discussed relating to the war presidencies.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And you refer to decision -- conclusion 8, the first decision referred to is a decision on the establishment of the first Serbian elite units.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could turn to page 2. You've also highlighted the name of Dr. Branko Djeric, and under his name, the portion: "To report to the government on detainees and propose measures."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we see another reference to the issue of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And in that connection, can we turn, please, to tabs 159 and 160. Tab 159 contains instructions on the treatment of captured persons, and tab 160 contains an order on applying the international laws of war in the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first document is in order -- an order, yes, issued by the Presidency and signed by Dr. Karadzic, as president of the Presidency. It is dated in the gazette the 13th of May. However, in the original signed copy which we have in this case, there is a difference in the dating, and in the signed copy the date is given as the 13th of June. This order was in fact published in the gazette on the 13th of June, together with another document which we may be seeing on the same issue, instructions issued by Colonel Subotic, as minister of defence, and that document also bears the date of the 13th of June. And in the preamble to that document, the instructions, it refers to the order of the Presidency of the 13th of June. So I'm certain that the actual date of this order signed by Dr. Karadzic should be the 13th of June rather than the 13th of May, as printed in the gazette.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn next to tab 165, Your Honours. This is a session of the Presidency held on 17 June 1992. And it is headed, "Minutes of the 8th Session of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of BH held during an imminent threat of war on 17 June 1992." You've highlighted the list of attendees. The second paragraph of the document, which states that: "The Presidency was briefed on the situation on the front, particularly in Ilijas and Hadzici, where enemy forces viciously attacked our army positions the day before and once against, as many times before, violated the truce." You've highlighted number 3: "That the government draft decision on the establishment of a state documentation centre which will gather all genuine documents on crimes committed against the Serbian people during this war."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And number 7, the conclusion that: "Two state delegations be formed to visit Eastern Herzegovina and Bijeljina as soon as possible," followed by the composition of the delegations.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I would also call the Court's attention here to the fact which I won't mention from here on in, unless there's a change, that with the Presidency session, the number indicating the session has been inserted by hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, turning next to tab 169, which contain minutes entitled, "Minutes of the 12th Session of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina held during an imminent threat of war on 27 June 1992."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I've got the 11th Session, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. Wrong document on screen and I was reading off of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This document contained in tab 169 is indeed the 11th session as His Honour indicated headed, "Minutes of the 11th Session of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of BH held during an imminent threat of war on 25 June 1992." The first page you've highlighted a list of attendees, and in the second page you have highlighted item D that: "Working bodies of the Presidency be set up at the following session and that authority and responsibilities be precisely divided among the members of the Presidency."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn next to tab 171. This is the document that was on screen a moment ago, minutes of the 12th Session of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina held during an imminent threat of war on 27 June 1992. Mr. Treanor, you've highlighted the list of attendees and the first three paragraphs after -- or of item number 3, which indicate that the Main Staff of the army of the Serbian Republic of BH is ordered to cease all artillery and infantry operations in the suburb of Dobrinja immediately." The order -- the next paragraph indicates that: "The order is given to dig in and move from offensive to defensive positions. The Main Staff is also warned in the order of the political consequences if this order is neglected." And the final highlighted paragraph or sentence is that: "Fire should be opened only for necessary defence and only after informing the Presidency, the Supreme Command, and UNPROFOR, as mediators in the action of opening the airport."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I'd like to point out in connection with this set of minutes and the previous set of minutes and perhaps some other ones we're going to see that the number of the session has been typed in in the original. However, the second numeral, in this case, a 2, has been inserted or written over what was originally there in hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we could move next to tab 172.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Tab 172 contains the minutes of the 14th Session of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina held during an imminent threat of war on 3 July 1992. You've highlighted, Mr. Treanor, the attendees of that session.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And then you've highlighted item 2.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we see the Presidency dealing with matters relating to the Ministry of Internal Affairs. There is, in fact, a written order by the Presidency, a copy of which we possess, signed by Dr. Karadzic, relating to this particular matter of the paramilitary units in Gacko and Nevesinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we could turn next to tab 173, which is the document contained at 173 is headed, "Minutes of the 36th Session of the Serb Republic of BH government held on the 4th of July, 1992."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, you've highlighted on page 2 of that document item number 1.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These type of numbers refer to the number of the item on the agenda.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And you've highlighted the first two sentences, or first full paragraph of that agenda item, which indicate that: "The minutes of the joint session of the Serb Republic of BH Presidency and Serb Republic of BH government held on the 1st of July, 1992 has been adopted in its proposed version." And it goes on to note that: "It has been concluded that the minutes be submitted to the members of the Presidency and the Serb Republic of BH Army Main Staff."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now, if I'm not mistaken, this is a session which we do not have any other record of, that is, the session that's referred to here on the 1st of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn next to page 4. You've highlighted agenda item number 8, which appears at the bottom of the page and continues on to the next page.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This agenda item indicates that: "The question has been raised whether there are agreed criteria regarding the moving out of the Muslims [sic] population from the territory of the Serb Republic of BH." And continues: "It has been concluded that the government has not until now had a point of view on this matter. The Ministry of the Interior is entrusted with preparing information on this issue that the government would consider and take the appropriate standpoint."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And we are not in possession of any such information that may have been produced by the Ministry of Internal Affairs on that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Turning to tab 174. That portion of the binder contains a document headed, "Minutes of the 15th Session of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina held during an imminent threat of war." Mr. Treanor, you've highlighted the list of attendees, agenda item number 1, which is the question of Dr. Koljevic's participation in the work of the Presidency, and agenda item number 4, division of the tasks in the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We now see on screen, on page 2, a highlighted portion reflecting Dr. Karadzic's remarks. Is that part of the discussion --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Dr. Koljevic was expressing some dissatisfaction with the way things had been going with the work of the Presidency, and Dr. Karadzic is responding to that here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The highlighted portion reads: "It was important that we existed, even if we did nothing, because the Presidency was a symbol of the statehood of the Serbian Republic of BH, said Dr. Karadzic."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And can you provide us with some concise explanation or summary of the discussion that surrounded Dr. -- the issue of Dr. Koljevic's concerns, or is that sufficiently reflected in the document itself?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that's reflected in the document. He was contemplating, in fact, resigning at this point, but he was dissuaded from doing so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, on page 3, you've highlighted items 4 and 5, which refer to the division of tasks.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We saw this referred to in an earlier session, and here we see division of tasks within the Presidency, with particular fields of activity being assigned to, as I said, what I believe to be the five members of the Presidency at this point. It further stipulates whenever a member of the Presidency is absent, he shall be replaced by a member present at the session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For the record, item number 4 addresses the division of tasks among members of the Presidency. Item number 5 indicates that: "The following was concluded, that a platform for talks with the leadership of Serbia be prepared by the government of SBH; and that a two-stage meeting with state and political leadership of the Republic of Serbia be arranged. The first meeting should be with Slobodan Milosevic and on the second day, it would be expanded to include the government of the Republic of Serbia." And finally, that: "Dr. Karadzic and Momcilo Krajisnik were given responsibility for the first meeting."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If I could just comment on the last paragraph, item 4. I think what the meaning of that is, is as follows: That if there's an issue that comes up in relation to one of the areas of responsibility which have been apportioned among the members of the Presidency and that particular member is not present to deal with that issue, then any other member of the Presidency who is present at the seat of the Presidency can deal with it. The Presidency, according to the decision way back in May, when the three-member Presidency was formed, was to have adopted rules of procedure for its own operation. However, we are in possession of no such rules of procedure, as far as we know, formal rules of procedure were never adopted. This is as close as we come to seeing how the internal workings of the Presidency were supposed to function, as far as the Presidency itself was concerned. That is, what they saw as the way to handle matters within the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could direct the Chamber's attention and Mr. Treanor's attention to tab number 176, which contains a document entitled, "Minutes of the 38th Session of the Serb Republic of BH government held on 11 July 1992." And Mr. Treanor, if I could direct your attention to page 6, on which you've highlighted number 3.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is discussion under agenda item number 10, which is current questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The highlighted portion refers to: "The formation of a work group comprised of the Government Deputy Prime Minister, Milan Trbojevic, and the representatives of the Ministry of Defence, Ministry of Justice, and Ministry of Health, Work, Welfare and Family, to prepare a regulation (platform) on the treatment of Muslims and other nations on the territory of the Serb Republic of BH. In accordance with this, the constitutional rights and obligations, international conventions on civil rights, and freedom that oblige us have to be taken into consideration." And the next sentence is: "A larger debate would have to be held on the proposed document exclusively at the session of the Assembly of the Serb Nation of BH."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is one of the few if not the only reference we see to this particular issue in the minutes of government sessions, or indeed Presidency sessions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn to tab 178. This is a Presidency session held on 13 July 1992. Again, the first portion of that document highlighted by Mr. Treanor is the list of attendees, which include Dr. Karadzic, Dr. Plavsic, Dr. Koljevic, Mr. Krajisnik, Dr. Djeric, General Mladic, and General Milan Gvero. And in addition, on that first page, Mr. Treanor, you've highlighted item 1 and the first three paragraphs of item 2.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we can see the Presidency dealing with international Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. affairs and military affairs. This is one of the not very large number of sessions at which General Mladic and members of his staff are indicated as being present. That information is indicated in the appendix to the report I referred to earlier. I believe that's Appendix 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, because the next document will involve a new binder, this might be an appropriate time for the break, and we can avoid a disruption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll adjourn until a quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honours, if we could turn now to tab 181. That contains a session of the Presidency held on 24 July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, the minutes of that session are very brief. You've highlighted them in their entirety. And they indicate that: "After the briefing on the situation in the territory of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Presidency adopted the following: 1. Decision on the establishment and jurisdiction of military disciplinary courts; and 2. Decree on the appointment of the president and judges of military disciplinary courts, military disciplinary prosecutors and their deputies and secretaries of military disciplinary courts."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we see the Presidency dealing with issues of military discipline.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn now to tab 182, to the 17th Session of the RS People's Assembly held from 24 July 1992 through 26 July 1992. And before addressing the portions of the Assembly session that you've highlighted, or those portions to which I'd like to draw your attention, can you provide us with some brief backdrop to that session, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the first session of the Assembly since the 12th of May. Perhaps for that reason, had a very long agenda of legislative and personnel items, many of which consisted of verification of decisions taken by the Presidency in the interval. And the first item on the agenda was a report by Dr. Karadzic on the political war situation in the republic, followed by a report of the president of the government on the work of the government up until that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As indicated, Mr. Treanor, I'm going to direct your attention to a few of the portions of that session that you've highlighted, the first of which appears on page 2 and reflect the remarks of Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is which page of the original?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. That would be page 1 -- I'm sorry. Page 2 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And depicted on screen now is page 2 of the English translation and the two portions highlighted: "I am proud to have enjoyed your trust in leading this Serb parliament and together with you, defending the Serb people from extinction." And then a sentence that follows a few sentences below: "Many of our people's brave sons and daughters have died on the Serb Republic war front, in an imposed war, war against slavery, humiliation, and extinction."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think we need any commentary here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 18 of the English, page 11 of the B/C/S. And here you've highlighted a portion of the remarks by Dr. Karadzic, and the highlighted portion reads: "We do not have any more reason to fight. We have liberated almost everything that is ours. In final talks we could even return some territories, villages, that do not belong to us."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In his address, Dr. Karadzic has been assuring the deputies that the Bosnian Serbs were approaching the achievement of their goals.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Turning to page 31 of the English, page 16 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. Which page of the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Page 31 of the B/C/S. To clarify, I originally indicated it was page 16. It is page 31 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we have Dr. Milovan Milanovic speaking, who was not only a deputy, but the vice-president of the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The highlighted portion reads: "We have a huge problem with captured peoples of other nationalities. We have hundreds and thousands of these prisoners."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think we need any commentary here. Again, a reference to the issue of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could direct your attention next, then, to page 49 of the English, page 50 of the B/C/S, and in particular, I'd like to direct your attention to the second highlighted portion of that page, containing the remarks of Mr. Krajisnik. That highlighted portion reads: "Our goal must be for the Serb people and the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina to reach their goal, their final goal, as one, the final goal being the formation of a state and a plebiscite, because that is the task of this people. If that is the aim, I must tell you right now that I do not care who is going to lead the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina today, whether it will be Karadzic, Koljevic, Plavsic, Djeric, Krajisnik, or whoever."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think that requires any commentary either.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the persons mentioned, just to clarify, Dr. Karadzic, Dr. Koljevic, Mrs. Plavsic, Dr. Djeric, Mr. Krajisnik, those persons specifically identified?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those would in fact be the members of the expanded Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could direct your attention next to page 65 of the English, page 67 of the B/C/S. You've highlighted portions of remarks by Mr. Prstojevic.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Prstojevic is from Ilidza. He was not one of the deputies elected in 1990, and I'm not sure if he's speaking here as a non-deputy or whether he might have been selected as a deputy in the interval by the Assembly, which itself, which did happen later. I don't think that's the case at this point, though. But as I've mentioned earlier, non-members frequently were present at the sessions and addressed the sessions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The portion highlighted expresses Mr. Prstojevic's recollections of the early phases of what he calls the uprising in Sarajevo and reads: "Namely, when the Serbs started the uprising in Sarajevo and when they seized control over certain territories, there was no government, or at least it was not known where it was then. Moreover, we even did not know if Mr. Karadzic was alive during the first couple of days. When we learnt that he was alive and when he visited us in Ilidza and encouraged us, the Serbs from Sarajevo retained control over the territory, and even extended their territory in some areas, driving the Muslims out of the territories where they had actually been majority."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think that requires any commentary.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And finally, if I could direct your attention, Mr. Treanor, to page 85 of the English, page 87 and then continuing on to page 88 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we have Dr. Karadzic speaking again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The first portion of that page that you've highlighted of Dr. Karadzic's remarks begin: "They want to keep us and the Croats in one unitary state so that we control the Muslims, and we cannot control the Muslims in such a unitary state. We know very well what the fundamentalism is and that we cannot live together. There's no tolerance. They quadruple through the birth rate, and we Serbs are not up to that. Not only are the Serbs not up to that, but the Christians in Lebanon are not up to that Oriental mentality stemming from Islam. Therefore, we cannot do that. Neither Serbs nor Croats together through the birth rate, the penetration of Islam into Europe, since in five to six years Muslims would make 51 per cent of the population of inner Bosnia."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we see reflected ideas which he has expressed before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The second highlighted portion which begins the sentence after the first, not the following sentence but the one thereafter, reads: "So, if they don't want any kind of Islamic state in the Balkans, then it is less likely that they will want a pure Islamic state, that is to say, an Islamic canton, a Muslim canton in Bosnian territory. There is truth in what Mr. Kupresanin has said, although nobody in Europe will say it openly, that this conflict was roused in order to eliminate the Muslims."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the reference here in these passages to "they" relates to the outside forces which Dr. Karadzic perceives as seeking to attain certain goals in BH.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And Dr. Karadzic continues, and you've highlighted a portion of that, which reads: "They think that they are being nationally established, but in fact they are vanishing. If that's the case, then we have our interests for our historical territories."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The "they" in this case being the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, I'd like to next direct your attention to --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: To tab 184, where the Presidency session of August 2nd, 1992 can be found. Again, Mr. Treanor, you've highlighted the portion of the session which indicates the attendees. Those were Dr. Karadzic, Mrs. Plavsic, Dr. Plavsic, Dr. Koljevic, Lieutenant General Ratko Mladic, Colonel Zdravko Tolimir. Apologies: Dr. Branko Djeric. And list the agenda: "1. Report on briefing on the conference on Bosnia and Herzegovina in London; 2. Assessment of the military situation; 3. Plan for further activities during an imminent threat of war." And then you've highlighted the first paragraph of item 1. That portion that you've highlighted indicates that: "Members of the negotiating delegation, who were also members of the Presidency (Dr. Karadzic, Dr. Koljevic, and Krajisnik) reported to those present that, at the last conference on Bosnia and Herzegovina held in London at the end of July of this year, they fully complied with the responsibilities stipulated by the Constitution and Law of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the authorisation of the Serbian Assembly which was in session at that time."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Could we scroll up to the top of that document again, the list of attendees? Mr. Krajisnik's name is missing in the English. It is -- he is listed as among the attendees in the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Treanor. The Chamber already asked itself whether this minutes were consistent with your report, especially the presence tables. We also see now that in the original, which is not in Cyrillic, but that Mr. Krajisnik appears in the first few lines, which seems to present those who were attending this meeting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. As I think I've mentioned, Your Honour, I and my staff work with the original B/C/S documents, and that is the basis on which we compiled our report. In many cases - and this is one of them - this is the first time I've ever seen the English translation, so I was a bit surprised at that myself when I saw it, so I double-checked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The translation seems not to be correct in this respect. This also draws my attention to what is handwritten on top of it, Roman numbers, in my view, represent 21 instead of 19 in this case.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. And the number of the session in the Arabic 21 is again written in by hand. In the original, an underlined blank space has been left to write the session number in, and that has been filled in by hand as 21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We've seen that in more of these minutes, even where you have not drawn our attention to it. I, for example, remember on the 11th there was also a handwritten filling in of the following order.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have drawn our attention to it under 12th but in the 11th it's the same, and I didn't check them all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And on page 2 of the minutes of that -- on page 2 of the minutes of that same session, you've also highlighted item 2, which reflects a briefing of those present on the assessment of the military situation in Serbian Bosnia and Herzegovina by General Mladic, in which he described the situation in each combat sector, the necessary tasks and the connection between ensuring material potentials and financial resources and the necessity of adopting the decision on general mobilisation. The item goes on to note that: "Due to security considerations and the detailed nature of the information, the conclusions and alternatives were adopted were not put on record." And finally the last sentence of that item indicates that: "The president of the republic shall issue an order proclaiming the introduction of a general mobilisation on the territory of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we see again the Presidency dealing with military matters, in this case, apparently particular sensitive matters, and this is one of the occasional number of personal briefings they get from General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn next to tab --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tieger, may I instruct you to provide a proper translation on that first page, because I made a note for myself, but of course, the official exhibit as kept by the Registrar has no correction to this translation mistake. So could you please provide us with another corrected page 00837962, and then a proper translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. We'll make sure that's done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, I just directed your attention and the Court's attention to tab 185, the next document. These are the minutes of a session of the Presidency held on 4 August 1992. And the portion of that document which you've highlighted is item 1: "The Presidency considered the situation at the front and discussed undertaking certain activities regarding the situation."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Another instance of the Presidency dealing with the military situation. Just to remind the Court, the Presidency is performing the functions assigned to the president of the republic and the constitution and the relevant legislation, one of which duties is that of commander-in-chief of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we can turn, then, to the next session of the Presidency, which Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. is contained at tab 186. By way of some backdrop to that session, Mr. Treanor, is it correct that at the beginning of August, Newsday reported allegations of Omarska camp and a separate camp at Brcko, and that on August 5th news reporters gained entry and visited the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, on the minutes of the August 5th, 1992 Presidency session, you've highlighted a number of items.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think we can go to the top on this particular document. Again, the list of attendees. Here we see specific reference to members of the Presidency, with five members being listed, Dr. Karadzic coming first as president of the Presidency, presumably.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could scroll down to the first highlighted item, which appears under item 1. That reads: "Regarding individual military units (brigades) which are in the territory of Banja Luka but are not under the military command, they should be placed under the central military command and withdrawn from Banja Luka."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a reference to the issue of paramilitary and other individuals, armed individuals, who were not under the command of the army or the police. Several orders were issued to the effect that such units and individuals should either disband or be placed under the command of the army or police.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm now directing your attention to page 2, item 2. You've highlighted the first sentence appearing beneath item 2, which reads: "The question of prisoners of war and their accommodation and the cost of food, as well as the question of political work in units of the Army of the SRBH, were discussed."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we have another reference to the issue of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And did those discussions about the prisoner issue continue in the subsequent two sessions of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know there was further discussion of that issue after this date, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn to tab 187, the 6th August session of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question. I see that where, on the 22nd session, it is still said that the meeting was held during imminent threat of war on the 4th of August, that on the 5th of August I do not find any similar, neither on the 6th of August, and the 24th, at least if I go through the binder. Is there any explanation for that, or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that you'll find some variance in that in the earlier sessions as well, Your Honour. I have no explanation for why the designation of the nature of the session varies from session to session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On screen now is the first page of the minutes of this session of the Presidency held on 6 August 1992, and you've highlighted the first portion, which indicates those who attended.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we see another list of attendees with explicit reference being made to the fact that Mr. Krajisnik and Dr. Djeric, it should read, were members.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 2 of that session, or the minutes of that session. And you've highlighted two paragraphs, addressing the issue of prisoners and war crimes. The first of which indicates that: "The work of the commission for investigating war crimes committed against the Serbian people in the Serbian Republic of BH and the former Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina was discussed." And the conclusion was: "The commission for investigating war crimes committed against the Serbian people will start, even if it is necessary to replace the commission members." The second paragraph addresses: "The treatment of prisoners of war detained in prisons in Serbian territory," under the discussion. And indicates that: "The prisoners should be divided into three categories: Those captured on the front; those who took part in arming and operations of the TO of BH; and those who assisted and financed Alija's army." And it continues: "It was pointed out that we should abide by international conventions in the treatment of prisoners of war. To that end, completely humane treatment of prisoners of war is advised because they are in prisons and not concentration camps. In wartime, payments for their food, clothes, hygiene, guarding, et cetera, are made at our expanse." The word in English is "expanse," but it would seem to be --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Expense," yes. I think we've seen reference before to the issue of investigating war crimes against the Serbian people and the establishment of bodies to do that. We don't see any reference in these documents to establishing any such body to investigate any war crimes that may have been committed by Bosnian Serbs against non-Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you one matter in respect of this document. The translation reads, "Signed and stamped." In the original, I have some difficulties in finding a stamp. Is that because of the quality of the copy or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not see any stamp on my copy, Your Honour. I do see a signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So it's signed and not stamped. Mr. Tieger, could you provide a proper translation, without any additions on this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We'll do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Turning now to tab 188, the session of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic held on 8 August 1992. Under item 2 on the first page, Mr. Treanor, you've highlighted three -- or five sentences indented, addressing the question of camps again.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we see further detailed attention being given to the issue of prisoners and camps by the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The highlighted portions begin with the sentence: "Special attention was given to the question of camps and ensuring a better information system. It was also concluded that in future all visitors to the existing and registered prisons must give notice of their visits formally and in time. In future, efforts must be made to agree 'all-for-all exchanges.'" The next sentence concerns the conclusion that visits by representatives of the International Red Cross organisation to all prisons must also be arranged. The next, that all prisoners above the age of 60, or those seriously ill or wounded should be released. And the last, the conclusion that an amnesty should be declared for persons who have committed minor offences or were misled into committing such offences.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, tab 189 contains the minutes of the 9 August government session. And turning to page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, you've highlighted agenda item 12. This item refers to: "The formation of two commissions consisting of representatives from the Ministry of the Interior and the Ministry of Judiciary and Administration. The commission's task is to gain knowledge through responsible state organs, about the status of people in concentration centres and other sheltering facilities; to speed up the procedure of categorising these people, establishing responsibility and sanctions."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here again we have the government taking an interest in the issue of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Tab 190 contains the minutes of a session of the government, which was also held -- or also dated 9 August 1992. And if we could turn to page 3. Mr. Treanor, you --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. This is a session of the...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This is the minutes of the 47th Session of the --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 20th of August. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry. Two designations. Perhaps you can clarify that for us.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document is dated the 20th of August. The previous session, according to the minutes, was held on the 9th of August, and the minutes are dated the 9th of August. This is the 47th Session, which, according to the minutes at the top, were also held on the 9th of August, but the minutes are dated the 20th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it help that in the agenda reference is made to the 46th Session of the government held on the 9th of August? So that there might be a mistake, since this is the 47th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's certainly possible, Your Honour. I am searching for a further document. Let me consult our report in this respect, on page 175.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just after the agenda, we find that the minutes of the 46th Session of the government were adopted. And the minutes of the 46th Session, which we found under 189, bear the date of the 9th of August.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. In our report, we discuss some of this confusion, which is -- discussion is very -- gets into some of the details. In fact, there was a 47th closed session held on the 19th of August as well. So I would conclude that this is the open portion of the 47th Session and was held on the 19th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect to the proposal to hold a closed session, we can turn, I think, quickly, to the same document we've been looking at, to page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor had previously highlighted agenda item 7. That item reads: "The government agreed on holding a special closed government session in which to discuss a report on touring of concentration centres and other detention facilities in Krajina Autonomous Region."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the issue of the dating, I would also add, as we indicated in our report, that the minutes of the 48th Session state that the 47th Session took place on the 19th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Both the closed and the open session were mentioned, and if I would look forward, I would find that in -- under tab 193, English text page 4, first lines reading: "The minutes of the 47th government session and the minutes of the closed government session, both held on the 19th of August, 1992 were adopted in their proposed versions. " That sufficiently clarifies the matter for the moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On the 11th of August, 1992, the 18th Session of the Assembly of the Serbian People was held. If we could turn, then, to page 191 -- sorry, tab 191. Mr. Treanor, perhaps you could provide us with the context and backdrop to that session.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the next following session, and it had a -- it took place not too long after the previous session. Its agenda is a bit shorter, consisting of a number of personnel actions, but also including the adoption of a declaration on the future state structure of the Serbian State of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Most of the other items in the agenda, the personnel items represent the confirmation of decisions taken by the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could direct your attention to page 2 of that document and page 3 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here we see deputy Marinko Kontic, who had been elected a member of the Chamber of Municipalities in 1990, addressing the issue of prisoners, which has been mentioned, became a subject of some public discussion at the beginning of August. And he is desirous of having this included in the agenda.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The highlighted portion are the remarks by Mr. Kontic towards the bottom part of that page, beginning: "I suggest you to include into the agenda the problem of prisoners. I think that our Assembly has never discussed about this problem and it is a very important topic. There are a lot of problems about it. That is the reason why I would like the Assembly to be informed about and to discuss it."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we turn next to tab 192. This document is headed, "Minutes of the 19th Session of the Assembly of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina held on 12 August 1992 in Banja Luka." And you've highlighted the items enumerated under the agenda.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We can see the agenda here, and I'd like to call attention in particular to two items. One is item number 4, on the future territorial organisation of the republic and the adoption of views on the regions. And number 6, which is: "Alteration of the Constitution and adoption of the Republic's name." The issue of the regions continued to be a topic of discussion until the following month, when, as I think we'll see, some decisions were made in that area. I won't go into that now. But I would just comment that at this time, an amendment to the constitution was adopted, changing the name of the republic to Republika Srpska, which is the form we generally use in referring to it. It could be rendered in English as simply a Serbian Republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Kontic's suggestion to include on the agenda the important issue of prisoners make it to the agenda?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think that was adopted as part of the agenda per se, although there may have been some -- the issue may have come up again later, in that session. That being the previous session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn next to tab 193, the government session held on 28 August 1992. And again, this appears to be, assuming the English translation is accurate, there appears to be a date discrepancy, which is relatively easily resolved by the agenda items.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the B/C/S, there is what appears to be an error as well. The date being given as the 28th of July. But from the numbering of the sessions, the date on the document itself, which is the 9th of September, and the content of the document, it would appear that this -- the date should be the 28th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Turning to page 11 of the English translation. I don't have the B/C/S equivalent. I think it's the last or second-to-last page of that document, and is agenda item 33.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's on page 15 of the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
