utterances.text: And Mr. Treanor, you've highlighted the first paragraph of that document before the bulleted items appear.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And here we see the government addressing the issue of prisoners again and specifying some action to be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For the record, that portion indicates: "The government decided Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to organise a meeting in Banja Luka on Saturday, 29 August this year, to include," and it lists a number of participants, including, well, specifically: "Milan Trbojevic, Dragan Kalinic, Bogdan Subotic, General Milan Gvero, Slobodan Avlijas, Stojan Zupljanin, and other Krajina representatives, to discuss the situation and agree the disbanding of concentration centres for prisoners. This should be placed in the context of implementing the decisions of the London conference. The ministry of information is due to inform the public about this and exploit it for propaganda purposes."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And just to remind the Court, the people mentioned are Mr. Trbojevic, who was a deputy and at this point also a vice-president of the government, Dr. Kalinic, who was also a deputy, and the minister of health, Colonel Subotic, who was the minister of defence, General Gvero, a member of General Mladic's staff, and Mr. Avlijas, an official in the Ministry of Justice, and Stojan Zupljanin, who was head of the security services centre in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could direct your attention next to tab 194 -- direct the Chamber's attention to tab 194 and your attention to the 27th Session of the Presidency held on 31 August 1992. In that document you've highlighted two portions, the first of which appears at the top of the page and the second of which appears at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we can see that Deputy Prime Minister Trbojevic, who was mentioned in the previous document, is attending this session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, in the English translation it indicates that the session was attended by the following members of the Presidency: Dr. Karadzic, Momcilo Krajisnik, Dr. Biljana Plavsic, Dr. Branko Djeric, Dr. Nikola Koljevic, and Deputy Prime Minister Milan Trbojevic. In the original B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is a minor discrepancy there. In the B/C/S, the "and" follows the name of Dr. Djeric in preceding that of Dr. Koljevic. So it should read Dr. Branko Djeric and Dr. Nikola Koljevic, followed by simply a comma, Deputy Prime Minister Milan Trbojevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This will all not appear in the tendered documents. Could I instruct you to provide a proper translation of this as well. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could scroll down to the highlighted portion at the bottom of the page, which indicates that: "During the session of the Presidency, General Mladic and General Gvero arrived." And if we turn to page 2.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They gave another briefing on the military situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And you've highlighted all of the minutes contained on page 2, which reflect that briefing and indicate that: "All details were discussed, but they were not put on record because of the level of their confidentiality."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And: "Certain conclusions were adopted on the basis of the detailed discussion which are not recorded here."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And this document does have a signature and a stamp, as stated in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we can move quickly through some of the remaining documents. At tab 195, the 27th Session of the Presidency held on September 1.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If I could just point out here. The Court may remember that the previous session was also numbered the 27th. On that particular document, the Arabic numeral is written by hand, as has been typical up until this point. Here in the minutes of the 1st of September we see that the numbers are in fact typed in but giving the same number as the previous session. And we can see that the -- in these minutes, the members of the Presidency are specifically referred to and listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And you've also highlighted item 4 at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we see a report by Colonel Subotic, the minister of defence, here described as the minister of the army, about military affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That item indicates that Colonel Subotic: "Briefed the members of the Presidency about his visits to certain towns and military formations in the Bosnian Krajina and the wider area and informed," it says: "The present [sic], of his military observations. And that the reports and conclusions of the minister were adopted in their entirety and he agreed with the order of the president of the Presidency regarding the engagement of certain military formations in the forthcoming period."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The end of the first paragraph should read: Informed those present.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could direct the Court's attention next to the -- sorry about the microphone. Your Honours, if I could direct your attention next to tab 198, the government session held on September 7th, 1992. Mr. Treanor, you've highlighted a portion of those minutes contained on page 5. Under agenda item 15.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And that's page 5 in the original as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That agenda item indicates that: "A government commission's report on a tour of camps and concentration centres in SAO Herzegovina was adopted."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Again, the government treating with the issue of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we could turn next to tab 199. This is an open-letter by Professor Plavsic directed to, as we see from the highlight at the top of the page, Mr. Boutros-Ghali, Secretary-General of the UN, International Committee of the Red Cross, Mr. T. Germond, the High Commissioner for refugees, coordinating committee of the EC conference, Mr. Jeremy Brade, and the French Red Cross, Mr. Kouchner.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could turn to page 2. Here, Mr. Treanor, you've highlighted the second-to-last paragraph of that page: "Some international institutions which have decided to extinct Serbs, give support to genocide. They do not think that, even tomorrow, the wheel of the fortune may turn around, the truth become evident, and that all those who supported the genocide may be lined up with those who committed crimes over children, women, and old people." And if we could turn quickly to page -- to the next page. The first sentence of the next page reads in capital letters: "Our Serb army do not rape anybody." And then we see the signature and stamp of Biljana Plavsic, member of Presidency.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the record, it's not the next page, but the second next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have to correct myself. It is ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it appears that the binder may contain --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- a duplicate page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In our binder it's the second next page but the next page is the same page as page 2. So it is on page 3, where the previous comment was on page 2. Could we just look back at the highlights we've just seen. Yes. One of the highlights was on page 2, and the next page was page 3. We removed the additional page 2 from our binders.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll just point out that the two page 2s are not identical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, they're not the same.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And in fact bear different ERN numbers. This was sent as a fax. I can see that the pagination of the fax transmission line is not continuous, so that was probably -- that page was probably sent twice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's sent twice, and I think for good reasons, because only now I notice that some of the lines legible on one of the pages 2 are illegible on the other page 2, whereas the same is true in the opposite direction. So reading two times page 2 gives us a full insight on what page 2 brings us. Please proceed. I apologise for drawing wrong conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, any further comments on that document before we turn to the next?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I could just make the observation that the highlighted portion on page 2 reflects some of the thoughts we've seen from Dr. Karadzic about certain outside forces being lined up against the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, the next document will be in the next binder. Perhaps while you're reviewing this, we can ... Your Honour, in connection with this binder, I should note, although you may not discover that immediately, that tabs 209 and 210 were intentionally left blank so that the B/C/S and the English could correspond.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn, then, to tab 201. And Mr. Treanor, if I could direct your attention to a government session of 26 September 1992. And if we could turn to page 9 of the English translation of that document, page 11 of the B/C/S. Here you've highlighted a portion that appears under agenda item 53, questions and proposals, and it's the first three sentences thereafter, beginning with: "The Ministry of the Interior is to prepare a report on security in Republika Srpska for the next session."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is under an agenda item referred to as questions and proposals, and it foresees another joint session with the Presidency. We've seen reference to such a joint session earlier as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The second sentence refers to a proposal for a report which should focus on the theft of socially and state-owned property. Do you know to what that refers?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. In fact, there's another inconsistency here. Socially owned property would be the property of -- under the socialist system of -- that was dominant in Yugoslavia until this time, what we might call state-owned property, that is, publicly owned property, enterprises, that type of thing. Public property, perhaps, would be a good word. And in the original, the next reference is to private property, which I don't think needs any explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn next, then, to tab 203, a session of the Presidency held on 9 October 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not entirely clear to me when you say in the original, the next --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The reference to state-owned property should be private property.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Should read private property. The Chamber would like to receive this page replaced as well by one containing the proper translation. If at least, and I'm assuming that, Mr. Treanor's translations are better than those of our translators. The Chamber has no view on that at this moment, but I take it that you'll seek the joint approval for the new translation, and once Mr. Treanor has -- well, perhaps it's better not to discuss it with him when he is not yet cross-examined. But I take it that the translators, of course, will have to approve the changes suggested by Mr. Treanor. If there's any issue which does not find the approval of our translation unit, then the Chamber would like to be informed. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, now we're looking at the minutes of the session of the Presidency of Republika Srpska of 9 October 1992. You've highlighted two portions. If you could explain that.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, again we can see highlighted the list of attendees, which again explicitly refers to members of the Presidency, only three of whom were present, Dr. Karadzic and Dr. Plavsic being absent, and in this connection I would call attention to the very end of the document, where the minutes are signed by Mr. Krajisnik as the presiding officer. And the document does, in fact -- the copy of the document that I have does, in fact, bear what appears to be his signature. Now, to get back to the substantive portions of the document. The term "Supreme Commander," I would render as the Main Commander, the reference being to General Mladic, who was the commander of the Main Staff. And this indicates that the Presidency would like to get information from him every day. As we've seen, General Mladic did occasionally attend Presidency sessions and brief the Presidency on the military situation. What other information he may have been sending to the Presidency in that regard, I don't know, but the Presidency evidently felt that it would like to get something every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And on page 2, you've highlighted the passage from the minutes: "Regarding the military operation in Sarajevo."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we see the Presidency taking a military decision. Again, the Presidency is performing the functions of the president of the republic, one of which is that of commander-in-chief of the armed forces. Again, the term "Supreme Command" might be better rendered as "Main Command." The term "supreme" having been used in the legislation to describe the position of the president of the republic in relation to the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, if we could turn next to the 16 June 1992 appointment of war commissioner by the Presidency, contained at tab 204.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document relating to the appointment of a republican commissioner under a decision that was taken by the Presidency on the 10th of June, one which I had previously selected but which we did not examine. But the main interest of this document is -- lies in the fact that, as the Court can see on the translation, it is -- it bears the name of Radovan Karadzic as president of the Presidency, and a seal, but it in fact bears what I believe to be Mr. Krajisnik's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could turn to tabs 205 and then 206, in succession. If you could explain those to us as well.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are similar documents, and they bear similar signatures, that is, what I believe to be the signatures of Mr. Krajisnik rather than those of Dr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you one thing. I see several times in the English translation, I see the word "for" which means not signed by the person himself but on his behalf by someone else. Could you guide us in the original where we exactly find such an indication in 204, 205, and in 206 it doesn't give a similar "for" in the translation. Could you tell us where in 204 and 205 exactly we find that. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I presume 204 is the 16 June document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 204 is the 16th of June document, the certificate where Mr. Jovanovic is appointed as the state commissioner for the municipality of Ilijas.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right. Well, Your Honour, I certainly could not definitely confirm that. I can see that by comparing the seals that there appears to be something written inside the seal, the stamp. In this case, at about 10.00 o'clock, above the cross, which appears to be a handwritten Cyrillic -- or could be a handwritten Cyrillic "Z."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if I may, Your Honour, this is the signature appearing on the document bearing the ERN 00903127.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The word for "for" in B/C/S is -- consists of just two letters, z-a, "za." It could be that that's what this is and the translator has in fact taken it for that. We see something similar in the 21 August document, number 3116, where we see something similar right at the tip of the cross. And in the third document, number 3106, if we could blow that up. There may be something of a similar nature at about 1.00 o'clock, just above the cross, over the writing in the inner circle of writing, there's a squiggle there, which again could be a Cyrillic "Z."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although there the interpreters have not interpreted that as a "for," because it doesn't appear in the ... Yes. It's -- at least it's clear to us on what basis we could understand that the translators have translated this as "for." Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, have you seen any other documents in which other members of the Presidency sign for Mr. -- for Dr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this point in time, I cannot recall specifically any such document. There may be one signed by Dr. Plavsic, but I don't have any specific recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll be guided by the Court on what time it wants to take a break. I'm not necessarily suggesting one; I just -- I know it will occur around this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We restarted at approximately 10 minutes to 11.00, so I would say that if we could have a break in approximately five minutes from now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could direct the Court's attention to tab 208, Presidency session of 26 October 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Treanor, looking at the designation of those present, or the indication of those present.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here again we see those present explicitly described as being members of the Presidency or, in Dr. Karadzic's case, the president of the Presidency. Dr. Koljevic also being described as a member, being indicated as absent.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 3, item 8. You've highlighted that item, which reads: "A report on rumours in Herzegovina about the behaviour of Branko Simic, people's deputy since April 1992. During his stay in Herzegovina was discussed." Its significance, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This relates to a fairly obscure set of allegations in relation to Mr. Simic, who was a deputy, had been elected to the Chamber of Citizens from Mostar in 1990, and I think we're going to see at least one more document in relation to this affair. At this point, we can note that this matter has come to the attention of the government on the -- I'm sorry, of the Presidency on the 26th of October. And the conclusion below it indicates that a letter should be sent to the organs of military authority to investigate the accusations of Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if you could turn to tab 211.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, that's a letter from Mr. Krajisnik to the RS Main Staff and dated 26 October 1992.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the letter which was apparently sent as a result of the discussion and conclusions reached at the session of the Presidency on the 26th to the Main Staff of the army, asking for an investigation in connection with allegations surrounding Mr. Simic. And the letter is signed by Mr. Krajisnik and bears his signature, with which we are by now familiar, and indicates that this document was adopted by the Presidency at its session of the 26th of October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am informed that, Mr. Krajisnik, you might not have a copy of 211.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I can indicate, Your Honour, we're just passing it across now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And Mr. Treanor, may I make one comment on what you -- on your testimony you just said, that we are familiar with the signature of Mr. Krajisnik. Of course, that depends on whether your suggestion that the other signatures are those of Mr. Krajisnik --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So could you please refrain from what is familiar to us at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And just before we leave that subject --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we better leave it, everyone having 211 open, for after the break, and adjourn until 20 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, we still have tab 211 in front of us. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honour, I appreciate your keeping that tab in front of you, but I think we can move on to the next item, which is contained at tab 212.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I apologise. I should not try to take over the lead. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And at tab 212, we find the minutes of the session of the government on November 17th, 1992. If we could turn to agenda item 22 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could we get back to that, the first page? 57th Session, 27 October. Yes. I thought you said November. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I did say that, and I apologise. You're quite right. I wanted to direct your attention, Mr. Treanor, to a highlighted portion that appears under agenda item 22, containing two paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here is another reference to the issue of prisoners in the minutes of government sessions, with information on this topic being obtained from Mr. Mandic, the minister of justice.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For the record, agenda item -- the highlighted portion of agenda item 22 indicates that: "Momcilo Mandic, minister of judiciary and administration, has informed the government on the situation in Republika Srpska camps and Assembly centres. It is concluded that the existing illegal camps and assembly centres are to be dissolved as soon as possible. The existing penal institutions legally formed in large centres in Republika Srpska are to be used, since the conditions there are suitable for legal treatment of prisoners and inmates." Your Honours, if I could direct your attention next to the following tab, 213, which contains the record of the 22nd Assembly Session held on 23 and 24 November 1992.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would start out by remarking that the 21st Session had been held at the end of October, from October -- from 30 October until 1 November, in Prijedor. We do not have any record, any written record of that session. It featured, however, an interruption for a joint session with the Assembly of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, that is, the Serbian entity in Croatia. That session was held with a view to some sort of union between the Serbian entities in Croatia and Bosnia. The session we're looking at now, the 22nd Session, again has a long agenda of legislative and personnel actions and most prominently, the issue of the resignation of the president of the government, that is, Mr. Djeric, who submitted his resignation around this time. A lot of the discussion at this session revolved around that issue. And one of the issues that came up in the course of discussion was the issue of the legal basis for the functioning of the expanded five-member Presidency, and also the war presidencies and war commissioners in the municipalities which the Presidency had established under similar authority to that which was supposed to have existed for the existence of the expanded Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, let me direct your attention first to a highlighted portion that relates to the first issue you mentioned, the resignation of Mr. Djeric. That's found on page 17 of the English, page 12 of the B/C/S, and the highlight reflects a portion of the remarks by Mr. Djeric. The highlighted portion has just been technically deleted from the screen, but it previously read, if I caught it correctly: "For example, when it comes to the justice system, when it comes to the minister of justice, the minister of internal affairs, they are not even in the government. They never come to the government sessions. Only to the president of the Republic or the president of the Assembly."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This appears to be one of the areas of Mr. Djeric's dissatisfaction, namely, that even as prime minister, his own ministers didn't come to government sessions and dealt directly with other officials instead.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention next to a highlight found at page 23 of the English, page 18 and 19 of the B/C/S, which contains a portion of the remarks by Professor Plavsic.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here Mrs. Plavsic refers, among other things, to her efforts to recruit volunteers for the Bosnian Serb cause.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And again, the highlight was briefly shown before it was somehow technically deleted and was the portion of her remarks which stated: "I tried to gather all those people who wanted to fight for the Serbianhood. You may talk about paramilitary formations and non-paramilitary formations, but, excuse me, it is none of my concern. I was looking for men who wanted to fight with the Serbs, on the territory of the Republika Srpska. Those letters have gone to the Soviet Union, and they went to Seselj, Arkan, and Jovic." They continue on to the next page in English, the first two lines of that page ending: "It is not small talk. I really did that. So condemn me," followed by applause. Anything to add, Mr. Treanor, before we move on?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't think that calls for much commentary. I think the reference to Jovic is probably to Borisav Jovic, who was a member of the collective Presidency of the -- what is at this point the former Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could turn next to the second issue that you mentioned earlier, and that is the discussions surrounding the legal basis for the expanded Presidency and the war presidencies, and that would be page 60 of the English, page 59 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we have Dr. Karadzic speaking and addressing that issue. I hope we can get it magnified.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As the Court can see, the process of magnifying the highlighted portion somehow is resulting in the deletion of the highlight, but I think -- I hope the Chamber had an opportunity to see where that was and we can nevertheless identify it.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It began with: "I was all in favour of the Presidency, instead of a president, because there was a lot of work to be done, and if Mr. Koljevic and I are busy, we have Biljana and, and if even she is busy, then we have Mr. Krajisnik." And it continued to the end of the next paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And in that subsequent paragraph, is it correct that Mr. -- that Dr. Karadzic describes the advantages of the expanded Presidency and the performance of the expanded Presidency?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, he says they discussed everything and it functioned very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And that portion of Dr. Karadzic's remarks which were highlighted indicate: "We have never come into conflict in the Presidency, without me or any of us being ready to give in. We put all ideas on the table, discuss them, and when we decide which one is the best, we go on."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could direct your attention next to a highlight found at page 76 of the English, page 75 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Which page of the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here we have Mr. Krajisnik interjecting during remarks by Aleksa Milojevic, who is an SDS official, party official, from Sarajevo, and at this point in time was the minister of development and spatial planning in the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We now have on screen the English translation of Mr. Milojevic's remarks, and a portion of which is highlighted, toward the top of the page. That portion says: "The citizenship of Republika Srpska is also acquired by birth at the territory of Republika Srpska, which, in fact, means that all Muslims and Croats who have been expelled have the citizenship of Republika Srpska." And apparently generated discussion from the seats. He goes on apparently to describe the article or proposed article about which he is concerned.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One of the proposals before the Assembly was a law on citizenship.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After Mr. Milojevic has expressed his concerns about the possible consequences of that law, does Mr. Krajisnik address the issue?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The highlighted portion at the bottom of the page begins: "We have decided that if this is Republika Srpska, it is Serbian, so that the citizenship is Serbian. There are no nationalities, just religion. That is the same as in France or any other country. That is why I would like to ask you, especially Mr. Mandic," and it continues: "I don't know who is," and on to the next page. Again, the highlights have been lost, but if I could -- I presume that highlight continued at least to the conclusion of his remarks there. But if I could direct your attention, Mr. Treanor, to the remarks by Mr. Krajisnik at the bottom of page 77, which I believe indicate the results of the discussion that took place, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. raised first by Mr. Milojevic and then followed by Mr. Krajisnik's responses. And if we could turn --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have on page 76 of the original, where it indicates that the draft law has been returned for further work to the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And we can see that in the bottom part of the first long paragraph of Mr. Krajisnik's remarks, where it is proposed that the draft law be sent back as soon as possible with the assistance of Mr. Milojevic and Mr. Radovic.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we continue on to page 78. At the top of the page there is a highlighted portion. I think we'll refrain from attempting to magnify that. That apparently results in some technical problems. As the first sentence of that page, Mr. Krajisnik's remarks: "I find that we have returned the Law on Citizenship to the Ministry of Internal Affairs to be rewritten with the help of Mr. Milojevic and Mr. Radovic."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's further down on page 76 in the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I could direct your attention next to tab 214, session of the Presidency held on the 30th of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, you've highlighted, in addition to the portion indicating those present, item 1 of the session, which refers to: "A discussion held at the initiative of Patriarch Pavle, regarding an amnesty for a Manjaca prisoner.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. This indicates again that the Presidency dealt with even individual cases of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The second sentence of that item indicates: "The amnesty is within the competence of the Presidency."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And apparently the conclusion is to request from Colonel Tolimir additional information about the prisoner.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn next to tab 215. I'm sorry. Instead of moving forward, Mr. Treanor, I do want to direct your attention to the second highlighted portion of the 30 November 1992 Presidency session. And that is found on page 2 of the minutes of that session and is item 3. And I note that on the English translation, two item 3s appear.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two item 3s appear in the original as well. It's the second item 3 is what is in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And that concerns a discussion about the justification for introducing a War Commission and an extended Presidency under the current circumstances.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is discussion in the Presidency of the issue of the legal basis for the expanded Presidency at the republic level and the appointment of war commissioners to the municipalities. As I mentioned earlier, this was discussed at the previous Assembly session. They're here discussing how to deal with this issue. As the Court can see, they recognise that the words "an imminent threat of war" would be needed if they were to simply -- if they were to go ahead and amend the legislation to permit the continued existence of the expanded Presidency. However, they wound up moving in a different direction, as I think we'll see very shortly, by re-forming the Presidency once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For the record, the second item 3 indicates, as I noted earlier, that in response to parliamentary questions, the Presidency discussed justification to introduce a War Commission, extended Presidency. It further indicates that it was established that: "For well-known reasons, a state of war had not been declared and that an extended Presidency, including the president of the National Assembly and the prime minister of Republika Srpska, could be introduced only under such circumstances. The case is the same with the War Presidency which was introduced to replace the commission." And then it discusses the law and amendments to the constitutional law, Republika Srpska, adopted on 2 July 1992. Describes it in the fashion you just did, including that: "The Presidency shall be extended to include the president of the National Assembly and the prime minister of Republika Srpska. The same law also stipulates that war presidencies can be established during a state of war." And then it goes on: "In both cases, if these institutions are retained, these regulations must be amended," and after the words, "A state of war," the words, "An imminent threat of war," need to be added, and after the words "war presidencies," the words "War Commissions." And then indicates that: "Each member of the Presidency spoke about his or her position and current work and the question of the introduction of the state council or the possibility of introducing two Presidencies."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now, just a minor remark here. The paragraph which refers to the War Presidency and the replacement which was introduced to replace the commission, I believe, should in fact read which would more accurately reflect what in fact happened. The same was the condition with the War Presidency which had been introduced -- which was replaced by the commission. The decision on the 31st of May had introduced the institution of War Presidency on the municipal level. On the 10th of June, a second decision replaced the war presidencies with War Commissioners who were also appointed by the Presidency. So the reference in this paragraph is to the war presidencies on the municipal level and their replacement by commissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but it's -- you've now reflected what, in your view, had happened, on the basis of the other documents. But the translation is correct in reflecting the original text. Because we should make a clear distinction on whether --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. In my view, the translation is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you then tell us exactly where --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the clause which reads here: "Which was introduced to replace the commission," should read -- I believe: "Which was replaced by the commission."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it really is a translation matter. Then, Mr. Tieger, may ask for your attention to it, especially for this page, and see whether the translators would agree that Mr. Treanor's translation is the more correct one compared to the one we have in front of us. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, the reference in the bottom of the highlighted portion, the possibility of introducing two Presidencies.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll look at that. The possibility of introducing two vice-presidents. As we will see, the five-member Presidency which was then operating was replaced on the 17th of December by a new set-up which consisted of a president and two vice-presidents, in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, it's on the same page, so it's ... Could you please take care that that translation is verified as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, directing your attention now to the decision on establishment of the Supreme Command of the army of RS, found at tab 215, Your Honours. We see two portions of that document highlighted, Article 2 and Article 5.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Article 2 describes the composition of the Supreme Command. And Article 5 indicates the -- something about the decision-making process there. The Supreme Command -- this is the 30th of November, after the discussion about the foundation, the legal foundation of the expanded Presidency and the necessity for some sort of change, this seems to be part of that change. A Supreme Command is formed, which has much the same composition as the original National Security Council and later the five-member Presidency, not exactly the same composition, but similar. However, the decision-making process here is such that the ultimate decision is left to the president in Article 5. And as I mentioned, they are about to reform the office of the Presidency once again and introduce a single president, so that instead of having a joint commander-in-chief, if you will, that is, a multimember Presidency exercising the powers of the president of the republic as commander-in-chief, there will only be one president and it will be the responsibility of that official, under Article 5, to ultimately issue any decisions which are made. This copy of the document is signed in the original, with a signature which can be fairly easily read as Radovan Karadzic. It bears the date of the 30th of November. However, it does not have a number. And as far as I have been able to determine, it was never published in the Official Gazette, as specified in Article 6. However, we do have minutes of one session of the Supreme Command which took place, I believe, on the 20th of December, from which we can see that this institution, in fact, did come into operation. That is the only set of minutes that we have, so I can't say anything about its functioning after that particular date.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn to tab 216, the 17 December session of the National Assembly held on December 17th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, that can be found in binder 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, I believe you've already provided some of the background to that session. If perhaps you could tell us what happened during that session, at least in terms of its significance to the subjects you've been addressing.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This session had a fairly lengthy legislative and personnel agenda. Most prominently under consideration were the adoption of a constitutional amendment and associated amendment to the constitutional law, which reformed the office of the Presidency yet again that I've already referred to, and this session also adopted a decision or resolution on declaring an end to the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn quickly to tab 217. We'll find the declaration to which Mr. Treanor just referred.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This declaration was published in the Official Gazette on the 18th of December. As we have seen, no state of war had ever been proclaimed. An imminent threat of war was proclaimed on the 15th of April, but a state of war was never proclaimed, although there are frequent references in the documents to war. And here we have a declaration ending the war, which is here described as the interethnic and interreligious war in the former Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And for the record, the highlighted portions include -- first of all, you've just referred to a passage from paragraph 1 of the document --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Paragraph 1 which is not highlighted, yes. Arabic 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And paragraphs 2 and 3, 3 continues on to the next page, are highlighted. And paragraph 8 also appears to be highlighted.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This paragraph relates to the prosecution of war criminals.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, I interrupted your explanation of the events of the 17th of December session, based on your reference to this document, but I should invite you now to return to your explanation about the session itself.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had concluded that. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if you could just indicate the persons who assumed the positions within the Presidency after -- or upon December 17th, or the position of president and the two vice-presidents.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Basically, the constitution was amended to provide for a president and two vice-presidents. But until the possibility of holding elections, the Assembly elected -- itself elected Dr. Karadzic as president of the republic and elected Drs. Koljevic and Plavsic as vice-presidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I could direct your attention next to tab 218 of binder 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This is the 24th Session of the National Assembly or People's Assembly of Republika Srpska, held on 8 January 1993. Mr. Treanor, if I could direct your attention to page 55 of the English and page 12 of the B/C/S. A few highlighted remarks or a portion of the remarks by Mr. Radic.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I could just say that this session was primarily devoted to a discussion of the peace negotiations that were going on at this point in Geneva. Mr. Radic is a deputy, had originally been elected to the Council of Municipalities from Ilijas. Here we can see him addressing the issue of the possibility, or it seems to be the impossibility, of the different communities living together.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the portion of Mr. Radic's remarks which you have highlighted appear toward the top of the page and read: "Believe me when I say that we cannot live together any more. I don't know under what conditions we could live together now. I have to be honest and say that they caused so much evil to us, and this time we did not cause less evil for them either."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could direct your attention next to page 79 of that session, page 20 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, was there a problem or ...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Something the Prosecutor said, page 12, but on page 12 we see Mr. Mladic speaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was already a bit surprised that page 55 would correspond to page 12, because you need very dense script. Could you perhaps verify, Mr. Tieger, where to find the ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The session could be in two parts and the second part numbered separately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That seems to be correct. Mr. Krajisnik, we have a second start of numbering pages, and on the top of page 12 in the second part, it seems to me that Mr. Radic starts speaking. You've found it? Please proceed, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The highlighted portion referred to now also appears in that second part of the B/C/S, at page 30 of that second part, and page 79 of the English. Now, the highlighted portion here indicates remarks by

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: "Savo, let me just explain why it isn't good. They want Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. us to say that we are all the same. They really want to create one nation, that we were all the same, only of different religion. We must say that we are different, that they are a group of Turkish orientation." And --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a comment on remarks by Savo Knezevic, who we have met before. He is a Serbian Orthodox priest, as well as being a deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the subject under discussion, Mr. Treanor? Perhaps before that it would be better for the record to continue at least the highlighted portion that I indicated before. That portion continues on to the next page of the English translation, beginning: "Well, all right, people, if we accept that they are some kind of a group, Turkish or I don't know whose, then we simply give them aces to their hands to be an independent nation. They will be more than happy to claim that they are of Turkish origin, the same as the Siptars, develop theories that they are of Iliric origin. Why, we should tell them what they really are. They are unbelievers, a nation that is not a nation, that is to say, a nation that would like to be a nation but has no arguments for a nation." And with that --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As the Court can see below, Mr. Knezevic has a similar view, saying that if they once used to be Serbs, as many people argue, they're not any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Knezevic's remarks appear immediately below the highlighted portion of Mr. Krajisnik's, beginning: "Respected assembly of the Serbian people, I think it is totally unnecessary and pointless to bring back to Serbism those who had left it." And concluding: "However, the speaker is correct, they are the sect. And don't let us bring them back to Serbism, please." And you've also highlighted Mr. Krajisnik's subsequent remarks immediately following: "Shall we then now take the Muslims out of Serbism forever. All right, gentlemen, can we now make up our mind and take a position that the Muslims as a nation are the communistic creation. We do not accept this artificial nation. We believe that the Muslims are a sect, a group or party, of Turkish provenance." Then he goes on to put those conclusions to a vote, asking who is in favour, who is against, or abstaining. And the highlight concludes: "Gentlemen, thank you, we adopted the conclusions." It says, "anonymously." I presume that's a translation error which should read "unanimously," but you'll need --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And this is a reflection of an idea we've seen before, that is, that the Muslims were at the -- at best a new nation and something invented by the former communist rulers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I could next direct the Chamber's attention to tab 242. In binder 16. I'm sorry. I erroneously indicated tab 242. That is tab 219.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just ask for the transcript, the last words by the witness is between brackets unanimously. Could you please -- I do not recollect you to speak this word. Or am I mistaken, Mr. Treanor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I interject when Mr. Tieger surmised that the word "anonymously" should in fact read "unanimously," and I interjected. Unanimously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I now understand. So "unanimously" should be, as a matter of fact, the first word you spoke in that answer, or is that wrong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I think I was interjecting at that point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- into Mr. Tieger's comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could focus on the transcript for a moment. The last line that I spoke I believe should read: "It says 'anonymously.' I presume that's a translation error. That means 'unanimously.'" And that is the point at which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's where it went wrong in the transcript. So we do understand that the word "unanimously," as spoken by you, is the last word on page 46, line 17. But paging might be a bit of a problem, because we started only halfway. But it has been clarified sufficiently, I would say. Please, then, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Turning next to an enlarged session --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Turning next, then, to a session of the Council for Reconciliation held on 9 January 1993 and found at tab 219. First of all, Mr. Treanor, we see here a body we haven't encountered before. Perhaps you can illuminate the Court on that before we look at the contents.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a council for -- perhaps the title could be more comprehensibly rendered as the Council for the Reconciliation of Positions on State Policy. The council is composed of members - I'm sorry - of representatives from the various Serbian entities, including the new Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, the Republic of Serbia, Republic of Montenegro, and Republika Srpska, and the Republic of Serbian Krajina, in Croatia. The president of this council is Dobrica Cosic, who at that time was the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Attending this meeting is a large group of officials from the various entities I mentioned, including Slobodan Milosevic, Radovan Karadzic, Nikola Koljevic, Momcilo Krajisnik, and Ratko Mladic. The basic task of this council is to coordinate policy among those various entities, in particular, in relation to the hostilities which are in fact still going on despite the declaration of the Bosnian Serb Assembly a few weeks earlier that the war was over.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, if I could direct your attention to a highlighted portion that appears at page 96 of the English, page 95 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here we have Dr. Karadzic speaking, addressing some of the -- some issues connected with the strategic goals which we have seen, indicating that the border on the Neretva was not nearly as important as the achievement of the strategic goals in the -- what is called here Podrinje, that is, the Drina Valley, and Posavina, the valley of the Sava River. That is the corridor which would link north-eastern Bosnia to western Bosnia. The paper being referred to is, of course, a paper that's being considered in the context of the international negotiations going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could turn next to a highlighted portion which is actually found earlier at page 94 in the English, page 92 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here Dr. Karadzic is responding to a remark by Mr. Mile Paspalj, who was one of the representatives present from the Republic of Serbian Krajina. He stated that they had never made any incursions into the Republic of Croatia and had remarked that the international negotiators were attempting to disarm them, in fact. Here Dr. Karadzic is advising him on how to respond to Croatian attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the highlighted remark by Dr. Karadzic reads: "You should invade them. For each person killed by a sniper, you should kill ten Croats. That is the only solution. You are entitled to retaliation."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see you looking at the clock, and I can also see that it's 1.45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I was looking at the clock. That's correct. And it's time to stop. I would like to ask the parties to remain standby on from 3.30 this afternoon. I cannot promise you that we'll start at 3.30, because this Chamber will first hear a plea on an amended indictment and then we'll have a status -- one of the Judges of the Chamber will have a Status Conference, which means that we cannot be sure that we could start at that time. But since everyone preferred to finish this Friday, and since it seems to be possible, because, Mr. Tieger, you've spent a little bit over 22 hours now on examination-in-chief. On the basis of your schedule, it should be possible for you to finish this afternoon. I see that both you and Ms. Loukas are standing, and apart from that, Madam Registrar would like to say something to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar suggests that the parties are all present in Courtroom II at 2.30, and you'll then be informed what to expect, whether we'll need another half hour or that we could start right away or that we need another 10 to 15 minutes. Yes, Mr. Tieger, Ms. Loukas. Did I say 2.30? Yes. And I meant to say 3.30. It's good to have an opportunity to make some mistakes as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So I take it, therefore, Your Honour, we don't need to remove our books and what have you, and folders, from this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because we go to Courtroom II, and we are now in 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Oh, we're going to go to Courtroom II this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we have to move everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Oh, I see. So everything has to be removed from this courtroom, and we have to appear in Courtroom II, and we may or may not begin at 3.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And of course, it would have been more comfortable to stay in this courtroom, but unfortunately that's not possible. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: There's just one further matter, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: -- if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Just in terms of the rest of the proceedings. Of course, the last document we looked at was dated outside the indictment period. Of course, just because something's dated outside the indictment period doesn't mean that there's not necessarily probative value, but I would be seeking that it would be appropriate -- for example, I think that the last highlighted portion was not particularly probative, I would submit, and if, perhaps, while we are dealing with a document that's outside the indictment period, that perhaps a little more attention could be paid to what's more particularly probative out of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you could use the break we'll have, you, Mr. Tieger, to explain to Ms. Loukas and to see whether you can convince her what the relevance is of the documents still to be presented and not within the indictment period. And if you cannot convince her, then of course we'll hear from Ms. Loukas, whatever objections she has in presenting this evidentiary material. Yes. If there's nothing else, we adjourn until 3.30 or later this afternoon, in Courtroom II. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.48 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This continues this morning's session, so there is no need to ask the registrar to call the case because it's just a break in the same day. I see Mr. Stewart, that you are back on the team again. Welcome. Mr. Tieger, are you ready to continue the examination --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of Mr. Treanor? Mr. Treanor, since it's the same day, I didn't give you any instruction when you left this morning. I didn't give you any reminders. Now you entered again the courtroom this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't need any, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, before we move on to the next document, I wanted to raise a matter that was raised shortly before the last break. We looked at the 22nd [20th of December] Assembly session held in November of 1992. That was contained at tab 13 -- 213. Excuse me. And one of the highlights was Mrs. Plavsic's remarks about paramilitary formations, her efforts to gather men to fight for Serbianhood and her sending of letters to Arkan, Seselj, and Jovic, and in that connection I think you indicated that the reference to Jovic might be to Borisav Jovic, member of the collective Presidency of SFRY. I wanted to clarify that because this Chamber has previously heard evidence about a paramilitary leader, head of unit group called the White Eagles in -- operating in Bosnia whose name was Mirko Jovic, and for that reason I wanted to ask you if you had particular information that the reference to Jovic was Borisav Jovic, or might indeed be another Jovic?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. I have to confess my knowledge of paramilitary formations is rather limited, so I was not familiar with that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could move next, then, to tab 220. That is the January 21st, 1993, enlarged session of the Council for Reconciliation, or Coordination, positions on state policy.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We've already seen the previous session of this council.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This is --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like to clarify that I'm not precisely sure who members of this council were since its formation is not recorded in any document that is available to us. We see here a list of people who attended. It is described as an expanded session, however, so it's possible that many of the people were not actually members of the council. Mr. Cosic is described, however, as the -- in the previous minutes, at least, as the -- let me double-check that -- as the president of the council.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we please stop for a moment. We have -- yes. It's -- well, I abuse the interruption for asking for one clarification. If we are talking about tab 220, Mr. Tieger, I think on line 16 of page 1 you said it was the 20th of January where I read the 21st. Is that any -- is that -- no. Let me just see. Let me just check again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We certainly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No -- yes. It might be 20 December. Could that have been 20 November. I haven't got the other binders with me at this moment, but Judge El Mahdi wondered if the 20th of December was the right date.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I will simply defer to the witness who I believe has the document in front of him. If not, we can double-check on the document itself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We are referring to the Council for the Coordination Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. of Policy.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The session we're considering now is the 21st of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just see whether -- I read on line 15 and 16: "We looked at the 20th of December Assembly session held in November 1992."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. That previous reference was to the 22nd Assembly session held in November 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 22nd. So December was actually the 22nd.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now it has been clarified. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And again, Mr. Treanor, and for the Court's benefit, although I'm not sure all the binders are available, we're at tab 220, the 21 January 1993 enlarged session of the Council for Coordination. I think you were just finishing some remarks about the membership of that council.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I cannot confirm, for instance, that Dr. Karadzic, Dr. Koljevic and Mr. Krajisnik were members of this council. As I said, the exact membership is unknown to us. Only the participants in certain meetings, and this one is certainly described as an expanded session, which seems to leave open the possibility that non-members attended, but I can say that this is only the second session that we know of that they attend, and the previous session that they attended we considered earlier this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can I direct your attention then, Mr. Treanor, and the attention of the Chamber to page 19 of that session, page 20 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are remarks by Mr. Jovanovic, who is a Yugoslav diplomat.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, the highlighted portion of Mr. Jovanovic's remarks begin with the second paragraph after he is identified as the speaker. In which he says: "Therefore, the territorial link with Serbian and Montenegro, in other words with Yugoslavia, has to be ensured in an indisputable way which is not transitory." Then he goes on to discuss what is more important and that is "to make the territory that we get nationally homogenous as soon as possible." And that continues on to the bottom of the page. Reading: "Therefore this should be the goal, not to change the topic of discussion, to the fact that a large number of Serbs have stayed on in foreign provinces." Then it continues to the next page: "We should grasp the territories capable of functioning and encourage the migration of our people in the direction of our provinces and others toward theirs. How to do that, that is the thing to be wise about. But this should be, in my opinion, our guiding thought. If this could be achieved it could be so as soon as in a couple of years' time." First of all, can you address Mr. Jovanovic's comments?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here he is addressing from his perspective the desirability of achieving ethnic homogenisation in order to assure the territorial links between Serbia and Montenegro on the one hand and the Bosnian Serb republic on the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, after Mr. Jovanovic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After Mr. Jovanovic expressed his view about the desirability and necessity of ethnic homogenisation and asked whether it could be achieved as soon as in a couple of years' time, Mr. Karadzic or Dr. Karadzic responded and that portion is also highlighted. He's the next speaker.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. And the places that he mentions here, Tuzla, Sarajevo, and Zenica are areas that were under the control of the internationally recognised Bosnian government, and in which there were still Serbs living who the Bosnian Serb authorities were anxious to see come and settle in the territories they controlled.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Further on on that page, Dr. Karadzic speaks again and you've highlighted that portion. And the highlighted portion reads: "I think that this which Jovanovic is talking about has already happened to a huge extent. There was 50/50 of us in Zvornik. The number of inhabitants of Zvornik is the same, approximately 50.000, and they are all Serbs."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now, here on the other hand, he is addressing a place which has been under control of the Bosnian Serb authorities for quite some time at this point, since probably April of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we turn to page 21 of the English, page 22 of the B/C/S, there you've highlighted a portion where Mr. Krajisnik addresses the issues that Mr. Jovanovic was talking about, and that highlighted portion at the bottom of page 21 of the English is: "Let me start with what Mr. Jovanovic was talking about and Radovan was also talking in that direction. The problem is not 45 per cent of the territory and whether it will be 55 per cent. The part they now took from ethnically pure Serbian territories and gave to others, that is the biggest resource we had in our territories."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here Mr. Krajisnik is referring to the peace negotiations and proposals for territorial division of Bosnia and the fact that under some of the proposals under consideration the Bosnian Serb republic would lose certain territories and that in the extent of those territories in his view is not the important thing but the importance of the resources that they would thereby lose.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If you could turn next to a portion of that session that you've highlighted contained on page 24. Some of the remarks of Dr. Koljevic contained at the bottom of page 24 and page 26 of the B/C/S. That's the last paragraph of that page which begins with Dr. Koljevic talking about the impression I have about our people, indicating he's travelled a lot around our Republika Srpska, and continuing to the bottom of the page and continuing on the next page. And the highlighted portion on page 25 at the top reads: "And we will have to develop the activity of settlement homogenisation while there's still time. Only these are our affairs. We will ask for your help when we need it. This is not for the conference."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here Dr. Koljevic in turn is addressing the desirability of ethnic homogenisation and the reference for the conferences, the peace conference that is going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I could next draw the Court's attention and the witness's and counsel's attention to video binder 23.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do that you're finished with this document, Mr. Tieger, or are you still in the middle of it? I had a question in respect of Mr. Jovanovic. Is he present in this meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Vladislav Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He speaks earlier in the meeting. He was the first excerpt we considered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I do not see him at the list of those present. Did he -- just wondering whether there are any mistakes in that or whether you would have any -- or am I mistaken? I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't see him listed either, Your Honour. He obviously spoke. Perhaps he wasn't of high enough a rank to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I put the question to you because it could say something about the reliability of these kind of documents as far as presence of -- Of course, perhaps he's not a ghost speaker, but I just wondered whether you have any additional information in that respect.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just directed the Court's attention to video tab 33, intercept binder tab 33. And as before, this is a video, and as before it will require a separate number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: May I just inquire, the CD has confidential on it. Will this be an under-seal document?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will then be Prosecution Exhibit number P70, and the transcript of the intercept will be P70.A.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a video taken from a collection of recordings of Serbian television made from -- made during the period July 1992 to January 1993 and depicts Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could stop that and restart it with sound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in this presentation, Mr. Krajisnik describes Bosnian Serb territorial claims in terms of the -- both the ethnographic -- an ethnographic map of Bosnia-Herzegovina and lines of military separation as they existed at that particular time. He claimed that the line of military separation coincided with the ethnographic map. I don't remember his exact terms, but that's the substance of his remarks. When the camera moved closer up to the map, it could be seen that in fact there were, within the military lines held by the Bosnian Serb forces, substantial areas that were indicated on the map as being predominantly or largely non-Serb in population. The map that he was using quite likely the map we see before us now. He described the desired borders largely in terms of the strategic goals which had been mentioned already, and he devoted quite a bit of attention to discussing the issue of the Neretva, which had not been achieved militarily as indicated on that -- the map that he was using. As can be seen in this map, for instance, in -- along the Drina, in the Drina valley, which was one of the important goals, we can see large areas of Muslim population. Up in the north along the Sava, even beyond the area that he indicated that they had not occupied, the small enclave, even outside that area there are large areas that are shown here as being non-Serbian. This again was one of their important strategic goals, to secure the corridor in that region. And in Western Bosnia as we will we can see large areas -- or some areas that were non-Serbian in population. So in fact, the coincidence of the military lines of confrontation with the pre-war ethnic map is -- was certainly by no means perfect. Indeed, far from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honour, the map on screen to which Mr. Treanor has been referring is found at the maps and charts binder, in tab 3 -- or 2. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn back, then, to binder 16, tab 221 to a record of the 34th Assembly session held on the 27th, 29th of August, and the 9th and 10th of September and the 29th of September to the 1st of October, 1993. Mr. Treanor, if I could first direct your attention to page 25 of the English translation. Page 22 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. First of all, I'd just like to point out as has been mentioned, this session took place over the course of a number of days spread out over a period of time of more than a month. The excerpts were -- we'll be seeing come from earlier in the session, that is from the August portion of the session on the 27th and 28th in particular. The session was later on in September, punctuated, if you will, by a sort of military mutiny that took place in Banja Luka in September 1993, but these excerpts come before those particular events. At this time, peace negotiations, however, are still continuing. The Vance-Owen Plan by this point in time was, more or less, dead in that form, but negotiations were continuing and modified plans were under consideration.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At the highlighted portion we see on -- at the top of page 25 reflect the remarks of Mr. Vjestica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which page in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Page 22 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the whole document here unfortunately. I thought Mr. Krajisnik was speaking at this point. But I don't have the whole document in front of me, so I can't confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, would it be possible for the usher to provide Mr. Treanor with a copy of the B/C/S we have here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is the end of a long speech by Mr. Vjestica, who we've met before and who is from Bosanska Krupa.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In the highlighted portion, as you've indicated, are the concluding three sentences of Mr. Vjestica's remarks, which begin: "And gentlemen, since it is written in this agreement that everyone will be able to go back to their own territory, that means that his people will be going back to Velika Babic, and we will have to compensate everything we destroyed and burned, and 17 mosques that we flattened. That means that with Babic, they will get Radic too. They will get everything. That is why I do not want to vote for that, and I cannot vote for that."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we can see here, Mr. Vjestica who is discussing the area, the situation in the area that he's from and is opposed to the idea of any agreement that would allow Muslims to return to that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could direct your attention next to page 33 of the English. Page 31 of the B/C/S. At the top of the page 33 of the English translation we see the speaker is Mr. Milinkovic.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He is a deputy, was originally elected to the Council of Municipalities and is also -- was also the head of the SDS in Rudo, the municipality that he's from.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The portion that you've highlighted begins at the bottom of the page, last sentence of that page: "Alija is offering and promising that everyone can go back to their homes." It continues onto the next page the first two sentences of that page: "Gentlemen, there is no Serbian state in Bosnian pot without gradual depopulation and relocating. If we want ethnically pure Serbian state, and we do, don't we? If we all know and emphasise that we cannot live with them, then we have to realise that these draft maps are offering exactly that and there has to be relocation."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here again we see a deputy advocating the idea of the maintenance Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. of an ethnically pure Serbian state.
