utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 48 of the English, page 46 of the B/C/S. Here we find highlighted some remarks by Mr. Krajisnik. It appears from the beginning of that, his comments on that page that he is reacting to the comments of a previous speaker.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Kasagic is a deputy from the Bosnian Krajina, that is the area around Banja Luka, and here we see Mr. Krajisnik desiring to keep that particular area ethnically pure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The highlighted portion reads: "Let me tell you gentlemen, Muslims and Croats ask for their municipality in Banja Luka which we did not accept because we must have that territory clean." And if we could turn to page 80 of this session in the English, page 84 of the B/C/S. This page contains remarks by Dr. Karadzic, and the highlighted portion occurs in the latter half of the page. It begins: "We are the ones who preserve Krajina the most. Look what has been stepped in from Krajina, 5.600 people from Kupres and 11.000 from Srvobrin [phoen]. If we let this happen. I'm hoping for what Mladic said that that actual state will be recognised, and the others who will lead to recognition will be blamed but that is all. There are 500 to 600 Serbs down south at Bihac, that is all. And we have preserved 250.000 places of the living space where Muslims used to live."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here Dr. Karadzic is referring to the possibilities for the influx of Serbs who are living outside of the area presently, currently at that time occupied by Bosnian Serb forces indicating that there is plenty of room for them to live within that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we to turn next to tab 222. Behind which will be found comments by Mr. Krajisnik at the 37th Assembly session. Highlighted portion of those remarks contained at page 4 of the tab portion would be the page enumerated 91 in the B/C/S, is contained in approximately the middle of the page in which Mr. Krajisnik says: "The factual situation is not like that. Believe me that the biggest tragedy would be if the Muslims accepted to live together with us. You saw how they were squeezing in with Croats but the Croats did not want it. We would lose our state. That is the only thing that I would not accept. I would accept, however that, we be granted a smaller percentage of territory than we have now, provide that had we remain separated and that we have our own state without Muslims."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And again, I'd remind the Court that peace negotiations were still going on and various plans being considered for different ways to partition the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If you turn next to tab 223.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, I notice that in tab 221, you made already a selection of pages which, looking at the total number of 466 might be a very wise decision. On 222, we did not even find a cover page saying what we find there. So we have to look that up. And the Chamber would prefer to always have a cover page indicating what this is, because there are a lot of chairpersons and there are a lot of speakers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And we'll take care of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, tab 223 contains a document entitled: Report on the work of the People's Assembly of Republika Srpska from October 1991 to October 1993.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And before I direct your attention to two of the portions of the document that you've highlighted, are there any contextual remarks or background necessary before we move on to those?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I could only remark that, as is obvious from the title, that this is a report that was drawn up about the work of the Assembly, and it considers the -- the work of the Assembly different -- over different periods of time, which it indicates, for instance, the pre-war period in the first few months of the war, that type of thing, and discusses the emphasis of the work of the Assembly during those particular periods.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And turning now to page 5 of the document in English, page 4 to 5 of the document in B/C/S. We see a highlighted portion that appears toward the bottom of the page and begins: "Most importantly the Assembly laid out the strategic goals of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina and appealed to the people to achieve them." And then it continues to the bottom of the page, ending --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This part of the report deals with the period in the work of the Assembly immediately following the recognition of the independence of Bosnia by the European Union. That is beginning on the 6th of April. And I think it takes -- takes this consideration in this section through September 1992, that is the -- considers the work of the 16th through the 22nd sessions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we turn to the next page, page 6 of the English, page 5 of the B/C/S, the first sentence of the third paragraph is highlighted and reads: "Besides permanently monitoring the situation and undertaking measures aimed at training and equipping the army and other state institutions to defend Republika Srpska, the Assembly also discussed the issues that represented a break with the socialist system prevailing hitherto in the former BH and Yugoslavia."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And this relates to the work of the Assembly during that same period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Finally, Mr. Treanor, I'd like to direct your attention to the 50th Assembly session held on 15th -- the 15th and the 16th of April, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Just before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Just before we move on from that document, I think it would be useful to know if the witness could cast any light on who prepared this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The 224?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. No. The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The next one to come or the last one --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: The one we just dealt with, before we move on to the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's the report with the handwritten "2" on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's right. It's got a handwritten 2. "Report of the work of the People's Assembly of Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us -- Could you answer that question, Mr. Treanor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All I can say about its authorship is derived from what is indicated in the documents itself at the top of the first page, the title page. It says "Republika Srpska, national assembly," and at the bottom of the page indicates that it was prepared or finalised in Pale, which was the centre at that time of the Bosnian Serb republic in October 1993, and it says the same thing at the very end of the document on page 15. At the end of the text of the document. At the end of the document you have a table indicating the attendance of deputies at Assembly sessions beginning with session 16.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you have no further information as far as the authorship and the source apart from the information you've just gave us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at this time, Your Honour. With the ERN here available, it might be possible to -- or it should be possible to determine where this particular document or the copy we have of this document was obtained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, I just directed your attention to the 50th session of the national assembly held in April of 1995 in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now, this is a -- was a very long session of the Assembly held over a period of two days. It had a -- a long agenda, but the main item on the agenda was a report on the military, political situation in the RS, and this developed into an extensive discussion of the state of military and political affairs -- affairs within RS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if I could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- Mr. Treanor, you said it was held in April 1995. I take it that in the B/C/S original, I see 15th and 16th of April, 1995, where in the translation I only see a month and a date. Is that a mistake, I take it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. In the original it does say 1995, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, a correct translation for this page would also be required.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would note that in connection with the Court's earlier remarks, we have added pages to this binder, in particular page 116 of the English. That was in response to remarks yesterday by the Court. That page indicates the presence of Mr. Krajisnik as speaker of this particular Assembly. That was an area of interest the Court expressed the other day when this session came up in connection with other remarks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Whenever a new page replaces an old one, could you please always indicate which tab of the binder it belonged to? Because otherwise we have to go -- Madam Registrar has to go through 224 tabs in order to find the right place where to insert it. So if that could be done. As I said before, we can make a note on our version, but of course for the record it's important we have the correct page in place. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe I should mention here, Your Honour, in connection with what Mr. Tieger just mentioned, in connection with this session and the sessions we just got finished considering, in particular the post-1992 sessions that we've been just taking a few excerpts from, as far as I've been able to determine, Mr. Krajisnik was not only in the chair at the beginning of the session opening those sessions but continued to be in the chair in those sessions during the period when the remarks that we have highlighted here were made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if I could then direct your attention, Mr. Treanor to page 145 of the English translation, page 176 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now here we have Dr. Karadzic speaking, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You've highlighted two portions of -- on that page.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This -- this is just before or within a page or -- a page of the remarks we saw I believe yesterday about the selection of General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the first highlighted portion begins at approximately the middle of the page: "At the moment the war began in the municipalities, where we were in the majority we had municipal power, held it firmly, controlled everything. In the municipalities where we were in the minority, we set up secret government municipal boards, municipal assemblies, presidents of executive boards. You will remember the A and B variants, and the B variant where we were in the minority, 20 per cent, 15 per cent, we had set up a government and a brigade, a unit, no matter what size, but there was a detachment with a commander."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is an interesting retrospective on the variant A and B document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The other highlighted portion on that page begins in the lower half of the page and says: "But it was the SDS which organised the people and created the army. It was an army. Together with the police, those who were the armed forces of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, they created the space, liberated and created the space."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And this reflects the importance of the police which we saw Dr. Karadzic emphasising at one of the March 1992 sessions where delegates -- some of the deputies were pressing for the creation of a National Guard, and he indicated that aside from having the JNA, the -- as its -- its army, the Bosnian Serb authorities had under their control the police, which were more than adequate, I believe he said on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, if you have nothing to add or no clarification required, then I have concluded my examination-in-chief of Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I have nothing else to add at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. Mr. Treanor, as you might be aware of, this Chamber will not sit during the next month and will start sitting again on the 13th of April. Most likely we will then start with the cross-examination -- with your cross-examination. So therefore, I just would like to be informed whether you are available on and on from that date, because it might take a couple of days.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. No problem, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then my instructions now last for a longer period of time. That means up to early April. I'm also aware that it's perhaps not that easy not to speak with anyone about your testimony that you have given and you're still about to give because of your position in the office of the OTP, but this Chamber is confident that you'll strictly follow the instruction not to speak about your testimony, not in a direct way but also not to have any indirect conversations on issues that were raised during your examination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I've been through this before for an even longer period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I just wanted to stress the importance of it. Then Madam Usher, would you please escort Mr. Treanor out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are there any issues to be raised by the parties? I would have a few, but I'd first listen to the parties, whether there is any issue to be raised prior to -- to adjourning for quite a long period of time. Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that opportunity, Your Honour. There is one point that we on the Defence team have been discussing and that -- in fact, it's a suggestion and it arose particularly in relation to the evidence of this witness. Where there are documents to be dealt with, we were wondering if perhaps it was possible -- I don't know if it's possible to have even a split screen so that the -- you have both the English and the B/C/S versions available so that in the sense the public character of the Tribunal is improved in that way and, therefore, the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. accused also has access to the documents in that way. So I don't know if the technology is available for that here, but it became particularly apparent to us during the evidence of Mr. Treanor and the voluminous nature of the documents, and I'm sure there are more documents to come from other witnesses, whether or not something of that nature would be possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What is immediately shown on our screen is that at least two pages fit onto the screen, but whether this could be pages of different documents is another matter. Mr. Tieger, would you have any information in that respect?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Only that of course that has been considered, Your Honour. We have experimented with it. I think much more expensive technology would be required and larger screens in order to -- I mean the more information you put on the screen the less can actually be seen, and under the current state of the technology, what we get is essentially two documents you can't read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I must say it's a bit surprising, because especially in all Windows oriented programmes you very often can fit two windows, so then you would have two programmes running at the same time. Of course, I -- I take it, Ms. Loukas, this is not a solicitation for getting all new screens at the Tribunal, but -- Mr. Tieger, you're --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I just wanted to say, Your Honour, I didn't mean that to be a blanket rejection of such possibilities. Of course we remain open to the best method of presenting the available information. I was simply trying to indicate that that was something that occurred to us before as well, and thus far we're not aware of a solution. We're happy to keep inquiring.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. We were just having a discussion --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Put your microphone on. That's the first lesson in technology.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. We were just having a discussion about that issue within the Defence team, and I think that we may have other suggestions we can come up with in that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber always prefers to have shared solutions, so since we have some time available until the 13th of April, if could you come up with a common solution that saves us time and -- why. Any further issue?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, of course, Your Honour, it's not just a question of saving time. It's also a question of ensuring that Mr. Krajisnik has access in the courtroom to all the relevant documents. But other than that issue at this stage, I have no further issues to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I hope that everyone has been aware that to the extent the Chamber could assure that Mr. Krajisnik has got the proper information as far as pages are concerned, or when there was a missing document that the Chamber finds it of utmost importance that Mr. Krajisnik can follow every single detail of what is presented in this courtroom. Mr. Tieger, is there anything you'd like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, there's not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then as I promised, I have a few matters, the first being, but it's just a simple question, I take it that when we receive certain pages of documents that the whole of the document is accessible to the Defence, Mr. Tieger, perhaps even disclosed. I'm not soliciting for getting also 3 or 400 pages of a document which might not on every page be that relevant, but I take it that the Defence has an opportunity to check whether who leaves the meeting, who comes back again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think that has been our objective with one exception I might note in the English translation, and that was we -- the portions of the speech of Mr. Krajisnik, and in that regard we took up the Defence on a suggestion made long ago to than late portions of documents, of extremely large documents that were considered relevant and would be admitted and the Defence could then translate portion -- any portion of the document that they considered should also be translated. That was the -- in fact, the origin of the Novi Sad project with which the Court may be familiar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So at least the original is available to the Defence so that they can identify other portions on which they would like to have translations in order to create the context necessary for the presentation of the Defence case and for cross-examination of witnesses. I have two other issues. First of all, I think we indicated before that the Chamber would very much like to have a short meeting with counsel in Chambers to evaluate all kind of practical matters, speed, scheduling, well, whatever, and wondered whether the parties, counsel of the parties, would be available for that somewhere next week. I'm asking because I can imagine that you have other plans. Mr. Stewart, your body language tells me that you might not be that happy with next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I don't know whether to feel encouraged or discouraged that my body language is so obvious, Your Honour, but at least it's form of communication. But Your Honour, the next week would be very difficult, in fact, but the week after, if we could identify -- I don't know how the Chamber's commitments are, but the week after if we could try and identify a suitable date that would be much more satisfactory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please get in touch, then, with the legal officer Mr. Acquaviva, who is present today in the courtroom and he will try to find out whether there is a moment where Bench and parties would be available. The other thing that's already an indication, there have been some problems in respect of the way the intercepts were played. What actually happens is that we hear the B/C/S original, we read on our screens English, and the English is not spoken. At the same time, this English is translated into French, and the French text being spoken by the interpreter appears in the transcript. That means that we have unbalanced transcripts because there is no English text in it, but there is a French transcript. So we have a lot of empty English pages just saying "No translation." This is not a very satisfactory solution. We all know that the English text appears in the exhibits, the transcripts of the intercepts, but the Chamber suggests for the future that if similar intercepts are played that after a short warning, everyone moves to the B/C/S channel so that we can hear the original language. We can read the English on the screen. At the same time, the English text is then pronounced by the English booth and is -- the text is translated into French and the French is also pronounced by the interpreters. As a result of that, we would have a balanced transcript where it would not be necessary to look at all the videotapes in order to find out -- or to look in the exhibits in order to find out what words were actually on our screen. This is just a suggestion, but it's one of the technical problems we faced, and the Chamber has decided not to change the system for the last one or two intercepts although we were already aware of that problem at that moment. I'd like the parties to think about this solution which guarantees that we have more complete transcripts of the court sessions later on and would better meet one of the standards in this Tribunal that every word appears in the transcript. Is there any other matter to be raised at this moment? And I'm not only looking to the parties, to the counsel, but also Mr. Krajisnik. Is there anything you'd like to raise at this very moment because you will not have an opportunity for the next five or six weeks.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. All I wish to do is thank you for making it possible for me to -- to follow these proceedings. I had for a long while been quite a passive participant in these proceedings, which was very bad for me. It would be better, though, if I could also follow the reading of the text on the monitor, which would make a great deal of difference. I would be better able in that way to assist my counsel as well. Thank you very much again, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the Prosecution has explained that, although it has no solution yet in mind, it will still reconsider whether it will be possible to have the originals, the B/C/S originals, also on the screen. This is not a guarantee but at least we'll look to solve this problem. Being there are no other issues to discuss at this moment, we will adjourn until the 13th of April. I do not know yet in what courtroom, but we've got only three, so the Chamber's confident that you'll be able to find the right courtroom. I know that it's not holiday, the next few weeks, that's true for everyone. That's true for you, I take it, Mr. Krajisnik. It's true for the counsel. It's true for the Chamber as well. So I wish you a very fruitful period of five to six weeks where we do not see each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 13th day of April, 2004, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.13 p.m.,
